Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › India and its neighbourhood relations › India-Bangladesh — Hasina passport request and extradition
CA Topic / Headline: Bangladesh asked India, via its High Commission, for Sheikh Hasina's passport; extradition versus a prisoner-transfer route is debated, and the Ganga Water Treaty expires next month. Bangladesh PM is Tarique Rahman. Why it matters: neighbourhood policy, 2013 extradition treaty, water sharing.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The Ganga Waters Treaty was signed on 12 December 1996 for lean-season sharing at Farakka. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1993077&reg=48&lang=2
• Sharing runs from 1 January to 31 May each year in ten-day periods; Farakka is the last control structure on the Ganga in India. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1993077&reg=48&lang=2
• The 1996 treaty is valid for 30 years with a provision to review after five years. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=67568&reg=3&lang=2
• A Joint Committee headed by Members of the Joint Rivers Commission monitors the sharing. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1993077&reg=48&lang=2
• India and Bangladesh have an extradition treaty (2013) in force; Article 6 lets a State refuse an offence of political character. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Bangladesh sought Hasina's extradition for offences allegedly committed before she came to India on 5 August 2024. https://www.mea.gov.in/rajya-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38984%2FQUESTION+NO404+EXTRADITION+NOTICE=
• [Provision] The 2013 treaty allows refusal for political offences, with listed exclusions such as offences under multilateral treaties. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
• [Data] India and Bangladesh share 54 common rivers; the Joint Rivers Commission is the key institution. https://www.mea.gov.in/images/pdf/india-bangladesh-relations-04-05-2012-press-release.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Without renewal, the treaty lapses after 30 years, leaving lean-season Farakka sharing without a legal anchor. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=67568&reg=3&lang=2
• [Way forward] Negotiate renewal through the Joint Rivers Commission and handle the extradition request via treaty channels. https://www.mea.gov.in/leta
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Ganga Treaty 1996 (30 years, Farakka, 1 Jan-31 May); 2013 extradition treaty; political offence clause.
[Mains 2027] Assess challenges to India-Bangladesh ties after the 2024 change in Dhaka. (GS2, 15)
[Link] 2013 Mains

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies › NHRC — Meta-UNICEF funding, child safety online
CA Topic / Headline: NHRC wrote to the Women and Child Development Ministry on Meta-UNICEF funding and child sexual abuse material (CSAM) concerns. Why it matters: online child protection and NHRC's statutory role under the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NHRC was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993, in line with the Paris Principles. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/NHRCbrochure.pdf
• The 2019 amendment lets a former Judge of the Supreme Court, not only a former CJI, chair the NHRC. https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleaseiframepage.aspx?prid=1579522&reg=3&lang=2
• The amendment raised members from two to three (one woman) and cut the term of Chairperson and Members from five to three years. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/AR_2019-2020_EN.pdf
• Chairpersons of seven bodies, including NCPCR and NCBC, are deemed Members of the NHRC. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/AR_2019-2020_EN.pdf
• The President appoints on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the Prime Minister. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/NHRCbrochure.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The selection committee has the PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Home Minister, both Leaders of Opposition and Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/NHRCbrochure.pdf
• [Data] NHRC has a Chairperson, five full-time Members and seven deemed Members. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/Overview%20of%20National%20Human%20Rights%20Commission,%20its%20functions%20and%20various%20activities.pdf
• [Provision] The Secretary-General exercises administrative and financial powers, except judicial functions, under the Chairperson's control. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/publication/Overview%20of%20National%20Human%20Rights%20Commission,%20its%20functions%20and%20various%20activities.pdf
• [Counterpoint] A three-year term with reappointment may weaken security of tenure and independence from the executive. https://nhrc.nic.in/assets/uploads/annual_reports/AR_2019-2020_EN.pdf

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Governance › Governance, transparency and accountability, e-governance, citizens charters, institutional measures › Sanction for prosecution — Prevention of Corruption Act 1988
CA Topic / Headline: Keralam's Governor sanctioned prosecution of ex-minister Abdurahiman in the Messi case, and the PMO sanctioned prosecution of two IAS officers in the ₹98.25-crore Tamil Nadu tender case. Why it matters: Section 19 and Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 19: no court takes cognizance of offences under sections 7, 11, 13 and 15 against a public servant without previous sanction. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1558/1/A1988-49.pdf
• The 2018 amendment asks the sanctioning authority to decide within three months, extendable by one month for legal consultation. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
• Section 17A (w.e.f. 26 July 2018) bars police inquiry into decision-related offences without prior approval. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• No Section 17A approval is needed for arrest on the spot while accepting or attempting to accept an undue advantage. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• The 2018 amendment extended sanction protection to persons who have ceased to hold the office. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2013/Prevention%20of%20corruption%20as%20passed%20by%20both%20Houses.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The appointing authority is responsible for granting sanction, and must apply its own mind to the material placed before it. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (13 Jan 2026) examined the constitutional validity of Section 17A. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• [Data] Petitioners cited that prior approval was refused in 989 of 2,395 CBI cases (41.3%). https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/40618/40618_2018_4_1501_67544_Judgement_13-Jan-2026.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Sanction shields honest officials from vexatious prosecution, but delay and refusal can shield the corrupt. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
• [Way forward] Time-bound, reasoned and transparent sanction decisions with deemed-sanction or review mechanisms. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2022/3264/3264_2022_15_1501_38812_Judgement_11-Oct-2022.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] PC Act Section 19 sanction; Section 17A prior approval (2018); three-month timeline.
[Mains 2027] Does prior sanction protect honest officials or shield the corrupt? Discuss. (GS2, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Constitution: historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions, basic structure › Preventive detention — NSA 1980, Article 22
CA Topic / Headline: NSA was invoked against Noida-protest activists, including theatre artiste Aakriti Chaudhary and journalist Satyam Verma; CaRWAN held a protest in Mumbai; the allegations are not independently verified. Why it matters: preventive detention, Article 22 safeguards, civil liberties.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Under NSA 1980 the government must refer a detention order to the Advisory Board within three weeks. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• The Advisory Board reports within seven weeks of detention. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• The maximum period of detention under NSA is twelve months from the date of detention. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• Article 22(4): preventive detention beyond three months needs an Advisory Board of High Court judges reporting sufficient cause. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-22-protection-against-arrest-and-detention-in-certain-cases/
• A detainee cannot appear through a legal practitioner before the Advisory Board. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] If the Advisory Board finds no sufficient cause, the government must revoke the order and release the person. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1758/1/198065.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (29 Sep 2026) heard a challenge to an NSA detention alleging breach of Article 22 for grounds not furnished. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2026/37437/37437_2026_6_1501_74756_Judgement_29-Sep-2026.pdf
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court (2024) warned that mechanical detention orders make the Advisory Board a vital safeguard. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/8159/8159_2024_1_1501_51616_Judgement_21-Mar-2024.pdf
• [Counterpoint] The Act allows detention to prevent acts, not punish them, giving the executive wide satisfaction-based powers. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/8159/8159_2024_1_1501_51616_Judgement_21-Mar-2024.pdf
• [Way forward] Insist on speedy furnishing of grounds, reasoned orders and effective Advisory Board scrutiny. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/8159/8159_2024_1_1501_51616_Judgement_21-Mar-2024.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] NSA 1980: Advisory Board within three weeks, 12-month maximum; Article 22(4).
[Mains 2027] Examine safeguards against misuse of preventive detention laws. (GS2, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Security challenges in border areas; organised crime and terrorism › UAPA — unlawful association ban procedure
CA Topic / Headline: The Union Home Ministry extended for five more years the UAPA ban on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation, first declared an unlawful association in 2016 and extended in 2021. Naik is in Malaysia; extradition and an Interpol Red Notice remain pending. Why it matters: UAPA procedure, terror financing and GS3 security.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• UAPA 1967 section 3(1): Centre may declare an association unlawful by notification in the Official Gazette. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• Section 4: Centre must refer the notification to the UAPA Tribunal within thirty days; the Tribunal decides within six months. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• Section 3(3): the notification has no effect until the Tribunal confirms it, except where immediate effect is directed for reasons stated in writing. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• Section 6: a confirmed notification stays in force for five years from the date it becomes effective. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• Section 13(1): taking part in or abetting unlawful activity is punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and fine. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Section 6(2) lets the Centre cancel a notification any time, on its own motion or on an aggrieved person's application, whether or not the Tribunal confirmed it. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• [Provision] Section 3(2) requires grounds in the notification but does not require disclosure of facts the Centre considers against public interest. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• [Example] The Centre declared four Jammu and Kashmir Peoples League factions unlawful on 15 March 2024; the Tribunal confirmed on 29 August 2024. https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-09/OrderJKPL_13092024.pdf
• [Provision] Sections 7 and 8 empower the Centre to prohibit use of funds and notify places used by a banned association. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Where privilege is claimed the Tribunal itself examines the material without disclosing it to the association, limiting the association's ability to contest the grounds. https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-09/OrderJKPL_13092024.pdf
• [Way forward] Ensure timely Tribunal adjudication within the six-month limit and reasoned review of renewals so bans stay proportionate. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1470/3/A1967-37.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under UAPA 1967, a notification declaring an association unlawful takes effect only after which body confirms it? (Tribunal, s.4)
[Mains 2027] Examine UAPA safeguards against misuse in banning associations. (GS3, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Executive and Judiciary: structure, organisation, functioning; Ministries and Departments; pressure groups › Supreme Court restructuring — Constitutional Court proposal
CA Topic / Headline: A Hindu opinion urges splitting the Supreme Court into a Constitution Court of about 11 judges in Delhi and four or five regional Courts of Appeal. The court held 92,318 pending cases at end-2025; Constitution Benches now decide fewer than 10 cases a year. Why it matters: judicial reform, Articles 130 and 136.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 130: the Supreme Court sits in Delhi or other places the CJI appoints with the President's approval. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-130-seat-of-supreme-court/
• Article 136 gives the Supreme Court discretion to grant special leave to appeal from any court or tribunal, except armed forces tribunals. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-136-special-leave-to-appeal-by-the-supreme-court/
• Law Commission's 229th Report (5 August 2009) proposed a Constitution Bench at Delhi and four Cassation Benches at Delhi, Chennai or Hyderabad, Kolkata and Mumbai. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/43789.pdf
• The Supreme Court Full Court on 18 February 2010 unanimously resolved that the Law Commission's recommendations could not be accepted. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=82669&reg=3&lang=2
• In 2016 the Supreme Court referred the question of a National Court of Appeal to a Constitution Bench. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2042983&reg=48&lang=2
• Parliamentary Standing Committee on Law and Justice reported on 7 August 2023 recommending regional benches under Article 130. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/judicial-processes-and-their-reforms
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Committee] The Standing Committee (Chair: Sushil Kumar Modi) saw Delhi-centric access as a barrier to justice; regional benches decide appeals while constitutional matters stay in Delhi. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/judicial-processes-and-their-reforms
• [Committee] Law Commission's 229th Report recommended splitting the apex court into a Constitution Bench and regional Cassation Benches handling High Court appeals. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=82669&reg=3&lang=2
• [Judgment] The Supreme Court has itself lamented that unfettered special leave petitions converted it into a mere court of appeal, contrary to the framers' intent for Article 136. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/43789.pdf
• [Counterpoint] The Full Court found no justification for benches outside Delhi in 2010, reflecting the judiciary's resistance to restructuring. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2042983&reg=48&lang=2
• [Provision] Article 130 already lets the CJI, with the President's approval, sit outside Delhi without a constitutional amendment; the Committee said it can create four or five regional benches. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/judicial-processes-and-their-reforms
• [Way forward] Pair any split with a case-filtering power for special leave petitions so docket pressure falls and the apex court hears fewer, constitutional matters. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/judicial-processes-and-their-reforms

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › TB — WHO Global TB Report 2026 and NTEP

• SDG target 3.3 includes ending the TB epidemic by 2030. https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/documents/tuberculosis/executive-summary-global-tb-report-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=cee1d35f_2
• RNTCP was renamed National TB Elimination Programme in 2020, aiming to eliminate TB in India by 2025. https://dghs.mohfw.gov.in/national-tuberculosis-elimination-programme.php
• UN held high-level meetings on TB in 2018 and 2023; 2023 funding targets are $22 billion a year by 2027 and $5 billion for research. https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/e97dd6f4-b567-4396-8680-717bac6869a9/content
• In 2024 India accounted for 25% of global TB cases, followed by Indonesia 10% and the Philippines 6.8%. https://www.who.int/news/item/12-11-2025-global-gains-in-tuberculosis-response-endangered-by-funding-challenges
• Catastrophic costs mean total TB costs above 20% of annual household income; the End TB target is zero such households. https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/e97dd6f4-b567-4396-8680-717bac6869a9/content
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] India accounts for 25% of global cases and 33% of the gap between estimated MDR/RR-TB cases and people enrolled on treatment (2024). https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/e97dd6f4-b567-4396-8680-717bac6869a9/content
• [Data] India accounted for 23% of global TB deaths in 2025, WHO's Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 stated. https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/726b4727-ac22-432d-96e7-563210b8fb32/content

• [Counterpoint] Between 2015 and 2024 incidence fell 12% against the 50% milestone for 2025, and deaths fell 29% against 75%. https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/e97dd6f4-b567-4396-8680-717bac6869a9/content
• [Provision] UN 2023 political declaration set coverage targets for rapid diagnostics, treatment and social benefits alongside funding and research goals for 2023-2030. https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/726b4727-ac22-432d-96e7-563210b8fb32/content

State drug controllers must submit action taken reports by 16 November; complaints go via the Pharma Sahi Daam app. Why it matters: drug price control, DPCO 2013, health access.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• DPCO 2013 was notified under the National Pharmaceuticals Pricing Policy 2012 and the Essential Commodities Act 1955. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1843838
• NPPA, under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, fixes ceiling prices of scheduled medicines in Schedule-I, adopted from the National List of Essential Medicines. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2116220
• For non-scheduled formulations manufacturers cannot raise MRP by more than 10% over the preceding 12 months. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2200938&reg=3&lang=2
• Paragraph 19 of DPCO 2013 gives NPPA extraordinary powers in public interest; it was first used in 2019 on 42 anti-cancer drugs. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1566632&reg=3&lang=2
• Ceiling prices were fixed for 935 scheduled formulations as on 1 December 2025. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2200938&reg=3&lang=2
• Consumers can check revised drug prices on the Pharma Sahi Daam app and the NPPA website. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2324743&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] NPPA found non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines carry average markup of about 170%, reaching 700% or more in some cases. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2321092&reg=48&lang=2
• [Scheme] The 2026 exercise covers 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs with trade margin capped at 30% of MRP, effective 9 November 2026. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2324743&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] The 2019 pilot on 42 drugs cut prices of about 500 brands by about 50% on average, saving about ₹984 crore annually. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2200938&reg=3&lang=2
• [Committee] Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilizers (6 August 2026) noted no timeframe to integrate permanent trade margin rationalisation into DPCO 2013. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/review-of-role-functions-and-duties-of-the-national-pharmaceutical-pricing-authority
• [Counterpoint] Companies must maintain production and supply of notified formulations to prevent artificial shortages as margins fall. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2324743&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Broaden NPPA's sales data beyond a private source covering about 70% of the market, adding hospital, Jan Aushadhi and e-commerce sales. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/review-of-role-functions-and-duties-of-the-national-pharmaceutical-pricing-authority
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under which Paragraph of DPCO 2013 did NPPA cap trade margins of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs? (Paragraph 19)
[Mains 2027] Evaluate trade margin rationalisation as a tool to make cancer drugs affordable. (GS2, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Agriculture › Farm subsidies and MSP; PDS; buffer stocks and food security; technology missions; animal rearing › PDS — ONORC and NFSA 2013
CA Topic / Headline: One Nation One Ration Card, launched in 2019, covers all 36 States and UTs with about 3.27 crore portability transactions a month and over 233 crore since inception, distributing over 614 LMT. SARTHAK-PDS has a ₹25,530 crore Central outlay approved till 31 March 2031. Why it matters: PDS reform, NFSA, food security.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NFSA 2013 covers up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban population, which at Census 2011 is 81.35 crore persons. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1977139
• Priority households get 5 kg foodgrains per person per month; Antyodaya Anna Yojana households get 35 kg per household per month. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2179514&reg=48&lang=2
• NFSA initial subsidised prices were ₹3, ₹2 and ₹1 per kg for rice, wheat and coarse grains; the Act commenced on 5 July 2013. https://dfpd.gov.in/WriteReadData/AnnualRecordUploadDocuments/b9c640b8-5889-4ffd-a62d-5b56c5d4f029_Food%20AR%202024-25%20English%20small%20size.pdf
• PMGKAY gives free foodgrains from 1 January 2023; free distribution was extended for five years from 1 January 2024. https://dfpd.gov.in/WriteReadData/AnnualRecordUploadDocuments/b9c640b8-5889-4ffd-a62d-5b56c5d4f029_Food%20AR%202024-25%20English%20small%20size.pdf
• Section 10 of NFSA: State Governments identify Antyodaya and priority households within the coverage determined under section 9. https://dfpd.gov.in/WriteReadData/Other/nfsa_1.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Scheme] ONORC lets about 81 crore beneficiaries take entitled grain from any fair price shop using ration or Aadhaar card with biometric e-PoS authentication. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2179514&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] ONORC particularly benefits migrant labourers and prevents duplication of ration cards. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2179514&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] About 80.67 crore persons were covered under NFSA against a maximum coverage of 81.35 crore. https://dfpd.gov.in/WriteReadData/AnnualRecordUploadDocuments/b9c640b8-5889-4ffd-a62d-5b56c5d4f029_Food%20AR%202024-25%20English%20small%20size.pdf
• [Data] In December 2025, 97.9% of transactions at ePOS-enabled fair price shops used Aadhaar authentication. https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2026-27-analysis-food-and-public-distribution
• [Counterpoint] Duplicate or bogus ration cards still hamper targeting; ration cards are being linked with Aadhaar and a central beneficiary repository is maintained. https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2026-27-analysis-food-and-public-distribution
• [Way forward] Extend coverage to about 79 lakh additional eligible beneficiaries and continue weeding out ineligible cards through updated lists. https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2026-27-analysis-food-and-public-distribution
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under NFSA 2013, how much foodgrain per person per month do priority households get? (5 kg; AAY 35 kg per household)
[Mains 2027] How has ONORC strengthened the PDS? (GS3, 15)
[Link] 2018 Prelims, 2021 and 2022 Mains

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Agriculture › Farm subsidies and MSP; PDS; buffer stocks and food security; technology missions; animal rearing › Fertiliser subsidy — NBS Rabi 2026-27
CA Topic / Headline: Cabinet approved Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for Rabi 2026-27 (1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027) on 11 November; Drishti reports a ₹62,370 crore tentative outlay, up 64%, DAP at ₹1,350 per bag and 20% sulphur cost reimbursement. Urea stays outside NBS. Why it matters: fertiliser subsidy and farm economy.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme has operated since 1 April 2010 for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• NBS gives a fixed per-kg subsidy on nutrients N, P, K and S; rates are revised annually or biannually. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• Under NBS the P&K sector is decontrolled: companies set MRP at reasonable levels, subject to government oversight. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• Government makes 28 grades of P&K fertilisers available through NBS; ammonium sulphate was added from Rabi 2025-26. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• Rabi 2025-26 NBS per kg of nutrient: N ₹43.02, P ₹47.96, K ₹2.38 and S ₹2.87; DAP ₹29,805 per tonne. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• Boron and zinc fortified or coated P&K fertilisers receive extra subsidy of ₹300 and ₹500 per tonne respectively. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] India allocated over ₹2.04 lakh crore in NBS subsidies across 2022-23 to 2024-25 for indigenous and imported P&K fertilisers. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• [Data] Tentative requirement for Rabi 2025-26 was about ₹37,952 crore, about ₹736 crore above Kharif 2025. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• [Scheme] NBS aims to align subsidy with global price trends of fertilisers and raw materials while encouraging balanced nutrient application. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
• [Provision] Cabinet fixes NBS rates each season considering international prices of urea, DAP, MOP and sulphur. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2334972&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Because MRP is decontrolled and only monitored, farmer prices depend on government oversight of company pricing. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/aug/doc202583598601.pdf
• [Way forward] Encourage balanced use of N, P, K and S through nutrient-linked subsidy and fortified grades rather than reliance on urea and DAP alone. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2211384&reg=3&lang=1
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which fertilisers are covered by the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme? (Phosphatic and potassic, not urea)
[Mains 2027] Evaluate the NBS scheme's impact on balanced fertilisation. (GS3, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India or affecting its interests › Quad — leaders summit and IPMDA
CA Topic / Headline: PM Modi to meet US President Trump and the leaders of Japan and Australia at the first Quad summit since 2024, in Manila on 17 Nov; the first Quad meeting in a non-Quad country. Why it matters: Quad agenda, IPMDA, Indo-Pacific, GS2 IR.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Quad came together during the 2004 tsunami response; elevated to leaders' level in 2021, with the first virtual summit on 12 March 2021. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Quad_brief_October_2023.pdf
• Formally the grouping is the 'Quad', not the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue; four pillars include maritime and transnational security and critical technologies. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Quad_2026.pdf
• Leaders' summits: Tokyo 24 May 2022, Hiroshima 20 May 2023, Wilmington 21 September 2024. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Quad_2026.pdf
• IPMDA was launched at the 2022 Tokyo summit to give partners near-real-time maritime domain data. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2057460&reg=48&lang=2
• MAITRI, the Maritime Initiative for Training in the Indo-Pacific, was announced at Wilmington in 2024 with India hosting the first workshop. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2057454
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Scheme] IPMDA helps over two dozen countries access dark-vessel data through the Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency, Southeast Asia and IFC-IOR Gurugram. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2057460&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] Wilmington launched the Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission, Quad Indo-Pacific Logistics Network pilot and Quad Ports of the Future Partnership. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Quad_2026.pdf
• [Data] Quad Infrastructure Fellowships expanded to over 2,200 experts, with well over 1,300 fellowships already provided. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2057454
• [Example] Quad Cancer Moonshot, announced in 2024, targets cervical cancer in the Indo-Pacific using public and private resources. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Unclassified_Quad_Brief_Feb_2025.pdf
• [Way forward] Leaders committed to secure Quad funding through national budgets and deepen interparliamentary exchanges so the grouping endures beyond summitry. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2057454
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which of the following are Quad initiatives? IPMDA (launched at the 2022 Tokyo summit); MAITRI (announced in 2024).
[Mains 2027] Quad is turning from a military alliance into a trade bloc: discuss with its maritime, technology and health initiatives. (GS2, 15)
[Link] Mains 2020 (Quad as trade bloc), 2026 (IPMDA and SAGAR); entry refined to the Manila leaders' summit.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India or affecting its interests › SCO — membership and India
CA Topic / Headline: Pakistan's Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in India, 20-22 Nov. Why it matters: India-Pakistan contact inside the SCO, membership, India's role, GS2 IR.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• SCO was established on 15 June 2001 by China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan; its predecessor Shanghai Five formed in April 1996. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-SCO_Cooperation.pdf
• India and Pakistan became full members on 9 June 2017 at the Astana Summit; India had observer status since July 2005. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/SCO_Brief_September_2022.pdf
• Iran became a member at the SCO summit hosted virtually by India on 4 July 2023. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-SCO_Cooperation.pdf
• SCO now lists ten members including Belarus; India assumed the rotating chairmanship in 2023. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2255790&reg=3&lang=1
• The 25th SCO Summit at Tianjin approved the SCO Universal Center for Countering Security Challenges and Threats and an SCO Anti-Drug Center. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-SCO_Cooperation.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India signed the Memorandum of Obligations in June 2016 and acceded to 34 SCO agreements, including the Shanghai Convention on Combating Terrorism, Separatism and Extremism. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/SCO_Brief_September_2022.pdf
• [Example] India's chairmanship theme SECURE: Security, Economic cooperation, Connectivity, Unity, Respect for sovereignty and integrity, Environment protection, articulated at Qingdao in 2018. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1918263
• [Data] After 2017 expansion SCO covered about 42% of world population, 20% of GDP and 22% of landmass. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1532376
• [Example] India joined its first SCO military anti-terror drill at Chebarkul, Russia in August 2018. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/SCO_Brief_September_2022.pdf
• [Way forward] India uses SCO to press zero tolerance for terrorism and greater trade, economic cooperation and connectivity. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2139116&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] India is a member of which of these: AIIB, MTCR, SCO? (SCO full member since 9 June 2017; Iran joined 2023).
[Mains 2027] Critically examine the aims and objectives of the SCO. What importance does it hold for India? (GS2, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2022 (SCO membership); Mains 2021 (aims, importance), 2023 (conflict inside SCO); entry refined to the civilisational dialogue.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Constitution: historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions, basic structure › Reservation ceiling and Ninth Schedule
CA Topic / Headline: Karnataka CM Shivakumar and Dy CM Parameshwara asked the Centre to put the State's 17% SC / 7% ST quota law in the Ninth Schedule, citing Tamil Nadu's 69%; the High Court on 12 Oct struck it down for taking the total to 56%. Why it matters: 50% ceiling, Article 31B.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 31B protects laws placed in the Ninth Schedule from challenge as violating fundamental rights; the 76th Amendment (1994) added Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation Act. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/f3b4ae82cc697454c66a98b610225f34.pdf
• Indra Sawhney (16 November 1992) held total reservations under Article 16(4) should not exceed 50%. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/f3b4ae82cc697454c66a98b610225f34.pdf
• Article 16(4B), inserted by the 81st Amendment (2000), keeps carried-forward unfilled vacancies outside the 50% ceiling of the year they are filled. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2004/scr1189070294_Scheduled_Castes__Scheduled_Tribes_and_Other_Backward_Classes_____Reservation_in_Posts_and_Services__Bill__2004.pdf
• Articles 15(6) and 16(6), inserted by the 103rd Amendment (2019), give EWS 10% reservation outside the 50% limit on Articles 15(4) and 16(4). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1806158&reg=3&lang=2
• Maratha reservation case (5 May 2021): the Supreme Court held the 50% limit crossable only in extraordinary circumstances backed by quantifiable, contemporaneous data. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Indra Sawhney (1992) fixed the 50% ceiling; the Maratha ruling (2021) refused to exceed it without extraordinary circumstances and data. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
• [Provision] Article 16(4) permits reservation for inadequately represented backward classes; Article 15(4) permits special provisions for SCs, STs and backward classes. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19150/1/constitution_of_india.pdf
• [Example] Tamil Nadu's 69% Act of 1994 was placed in the Ninth Schedule by the 76th Amendment to secure protection under Article 31B. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/f3b4ae82cc697454c66a98b610225f34.pdf
• [Data] Karnataka Act 1 of 2023 recites that the Government was satisfied of extraordinary circumstances to raise SC and ST quotas above 15% and 3%. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19594/1/01_of_2023_(e)_sc_&_st.pdf
• [Counterpoint] The Union told Parliament in 2021 it has no proposal to override the Indra Sawhney 50% limit, narrowing political routes to higher quotas. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1739434
• [Way forward] Gather quantifiable, contemporaneous data on backwardness and representation to justify any breach, as the Maratha reservation ruling requires. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/23618/23618_2019_35_1501_27992_Judgement_05-May-2021.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Laws in the Ninth Schedule are immune from judicial review: correct? (Article 31B; judicial review open after Kesavananda/IR Coelho; introduced under Nehru).
[Mains 2027] Can reservation exceed the 50% ceiling? Examine Indra Sawhney, the Ninth Schedule route and the Tamil Nadu 69% model. (GS2, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2018 (Ninth Schedule), 2019 (introduced under Nehru); entry refined to Karnataka's 56% quota.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India or affecting its interests › India-US — Pannun civil suit against Doval and Goel
CA Topic / Headline: A US court on 9 Nov let Gurpatwant Singh Pannun serve summons on NSA Ajit Doval and ex-RAW chief Samant Goel through Indian courts in his civil suit; the explainer asks if India can refuse. Why it matters: Hague Service Convention, sovereign immunity, extradition law.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Extradition Act, 1962 is the legislative basis for extradition from India, which also needs a treaty, agreement or arrangement. https://www.mea.gov.in/extradition-from-india
• MEA is India's Central Authority for extradition requests; Letters Rogatory and MLAT requests are separate channels for legal assistance. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/ISII_ComprehensiveGuidelinesMutualLegalAssistance_17122019.pdf
• India signed the Hague Service Convention; the formal method of service in India has followed it since 1 August 2007, per MEA. https://www.mea.gov.in/service-of-summons-abroad.htm
• Department of Legal Affairs is India's Central Authority under the Hague Convention of 1965 for service abroad of judicial and extra-judicial documents. https://www.doj.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/09/5526331464ba2e1608aeaa107a81d764.pdf
• Section 29, Code of Civil Procedure 1908 deals with service of foreign summonses and other processes. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/bitstream/123456789/2191/1/A190805.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Counterpoint] Extradition Act, 1962 places no bar on extraditing Indian nationals, so India's own practice cuts both ways. https://meacms.mea.gov.in/extradition-from-india.htm
• [Way forward] Contest jurisdiction on sovereign-immunity grounds and route evidence requests through treaty-based legal assistance rather than public confrontation. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/userfiles/ISII_ComprehensiveGuidelinesMutualLegalAssistance_17122019.pdf
• [Provision] MEA: Hague Convention documents cannot be served directly on defendants in India by a private judicial officer; service must go through the proper authority. https://www.mea.gov.in/service-of-summons-abroad.htm
• [Provision] MHA guidance: a country with a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty must consider serving documents, while non-treaty countries have no such obligation. https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-09/Guid_service_pro250309_4[1].pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which of the following is India's legislative basis for extradition? (Extradition Act, 1962; India-US Treaty in force 21 July 1999).
[Mains 2027] Examine India's options against a foreign civil suit naming its officials: sovereign immunity, Hague Service Convention and treaty cooperation. (GS2, 15)
[Link] First appearance — no PYQ yet.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Air pollution — CPCB plans to capture peak PM levels
CA Topic / Headline: Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav reviewed NCR pollution control: 191 non-conforming industries to be sealed, 233 congestion points, Multi-Lane Free Flow at 154 Delhi border points by 31 Dec; CAQM to prosecute officials after 30 Nov. Why it matters: GRAP, CAQM, NCAP.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• CPCB is a statutory body under the Water Act, 1974 with powers and functions under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2307658&reg=48&lang=2
• National AQI has six categories (Good to Severe) built from eight pollutants; the worst sub-index decides the AQI. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?relid=110654&reg=48&lang=2
• NCAP (January 2019) covers 131 cities; target is up to 40% PM10 reduction or the 60 microgram per cubic metre standard by 2025-26. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1909910
• A non-attainment city exceeds NAAQS for five consecutive years and has at least three monitoring stations. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983680&reg=48&lang=2
• GRAP was notified in January 2017 on CPCB's recommendation; CAQM, constituted in 2021, now publishes the revised GRAP. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989207
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Air Act, 1981 section 16: CPCB advises the Centre and plans a nation-wide programme for prevention, control and abatement of air pollution. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/7781/1/air_act-1981.pdf
• [Data] NCAP: 95 of 131 cities improved annual PM10 in 2023-24 against 2017-18, and 18 met the PM10 standard. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2036732&reg=48&lang=2
• [Scheme] NCAP earmarked Rs 19,614.44 crore for 131 cities (2019-20 to 2025-26): 49 via the XV Finance Commission grant, 82 via MoEFCC. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2036732&reg=48&lang=2
• [Counterpoint] Implementation lags: by December 2023, Rs 9,650 crore was released to NCAP cities but about Rs 5,835 crore utilised. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989207
• [Way forward] Track city action plans on the PRANA portal and keep grants performance-based on measured PM10 reductions. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2024/sep/doc2024924400701.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] NCAP covers 131 cities with a PM10 reduction target; GRAP was notified in January 2017 and CAQM was constituted in 2021: which statements are correct?
[Mains 2027] Why is air pollution in Delhi more serious than in other mega cities? Evaluate the CAQM-GRAP-NCAP response. (GS3, 15)
[Link] Mains 2015 (Delhi air pollution), Prelims 2022 (WHO air quality guidelines); entry refined to the NCR enforcement review.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Salient features of the Representation of People's Act › Electoral rolls — Form 7 deletions in Mustafabad
CA Topic / Headline: ECI told the Supreme Court in a supplementary affidavit how electors left out of the SIR roll can return: Enumeration Form (Annexure A) with Annexure B or C statements, Form 6, online via ECINET. Why it matters: Article 324, section 21(3) RP Act 1950, right to vote.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 324(1): Election Commission superintends, directs and controls electoral rolls and elections to Parliament, State legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-324-superintendence-direction-and-control-of-elections-to-be-vested-in-an-election-commission/
• RP Act, 1950 section 21: rolls are prepared by a qualifying date and revised before general elections and bye-elections. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2006/bill105_20070926105_representatiin_of_people_act_1950.pdf
• Each State has a Chief Electoral Officer (RP Act, 1950 section 13A) who supervises preparation, revision and correction of rolls. https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/showfile?actid=AC_CEN_3_20_00016_195043_1517807321506&filename=03_representation_of_the_people_act%2C_1950.pdf&type=actfile
• Article 324(2): the Election Commission comprises the Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners the President fixes, appointed subject to parliamentary law. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-324-superintendence-direction-and-control-of-elections-to-be-vested-in-an-election-commission/
• Article 327 lets Parliament legislate on elections, expressly subject to the Constitution, including Article 324. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17370
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Section 21(3) RP Act, 1950 lets the Commission, for recorded reasons, order a special revision of any constituency or part of it. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2006/bill105_20070926105_representatiin_of_people_act_1950.pdf
• [Judgment] Supreme Court: Article 324 operates in areas left unoccupied by legislation; its words are of the broadest amplitude. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17433
• [Judgment] 2026 INSC 564 (SIR): Articles 324 and 327 are complementary, and section 21(3) RP Act supplies statutory authority for special revision. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17370
• [Counterpoint] Plenary power is not unbounded: the Commission cannot defy an express statutory prohibition, so deletions must stay within RP Act rules. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci/public/api/document?id=17370
• [Way forward] Strengthen CEO and DEO supervision and record reasons for revisions; the existing roll stays in force until a special revision finishes. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2006/bill105_20070926105_representatiin_of_people_act_1950.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Article 324(1) vests superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls in which body? (Election Commission; RP Act 1950 section 21 governs revision).
[Mains 2027] Is the right to vote a fundamental right? Discuss the Election Commission's position in revising electoral rolls. (GS2, 10)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › Quantum technology — National Quantum Mission
CA Topic / Headline: Andhra Pradesh CM Chandrababu Naidu outlined the Amaravati Quantum Valley, aiming to put Amaravati among the top five quantum hubs by 2030; leaders stress linking research, industry, policy and talent. Why it matters: National Quantum Mission, State quantum policy.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• National Quantum Mission (NQM) approved by the Union Cabinet on 19 April 2023, outlay ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31; implemented by DST. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2111953&reg=48&lang=2
• NQM is one of nine initiatives conceptualised under the Prime Minister's Science Technology Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2111953&reg=48&lang=2
• Four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs): quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing and metrology, quantum materials and devices. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1997785&reg=48&lang=2
• Targets: intermediate-scale quantum computers of 20-50 physical qubits in 3 years, 50-100 in 5 years, 50-1000 in 8 years. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2115324&reg=48&lang=2
• Aim includes satellite-based secure quantum communication between two ground stations over 2,000 km within India. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2115324&reg=48&lang=2
• T-Hubs link 152 researchers from 43 institutions across 17 States and 2 Union Territories through 14 Technical Groups and 17 Project Teams. https://www.dst.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/07/3ffac728429fbdda48653688978fbdb3.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Scheme] NQM outlay is phased over eight years: ₹704.105 crore in 2023-24, ₹1,178.645 crore in 2024-25 and ₹1,260.985 crore in 2025-26. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2115865&reg=3&lang=2
• [Provision] T-Hubs follow a Hub-Spoke-Spike model linking institutions, so research, capacity building, startups and industry work together. https://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/Quantum-Safe-Ecosystem-in-India.pdf
• [Example] DST Task Force chaired by Dr Rajkumar Upadhyay prepared the plan for a quantum-safe ecosystem and migration to post-quantum cryptography. https://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/Report_TaskForce_PQMigration_4Feb26%20(v1).pdf
• [Counterpoint] Task Force warns quantum capability may advance fast while cryptographic migration stays slow and linear, a systemic risk to national security. https://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/Report_TaskForce_PQMigration_4Feb26%20(v1).pdf
• [Way forward] Mission Governing Board stressed manpower and startups; the Principal Scientific Adviser urged empowering Hubs to build human capacity. https://dst.gov.in/mission-governing-board-finalises-implementation-strategy-and-timelines-nqm
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] National Quantum Mission aims at 50-1000 physical qubit computers and satellite quantum communication over 2,000 km: which statements are correct?
[Mains 2027] Evaluate India's National Quantum Mission and the role of State quantum hubs in building a quantum ecosystem. (GS3, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2026 (NQM statements), 2022 (qubit); entry refined to the Amaravati Quantum Valley.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India or affecting its interests › India-Bangladesh — Hasina extradition request
CA Topic / Headline: Bangladesh's Law Minister Md. Asaduzzaman said Dhaka has completed all legal steps for the return of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina from India; the next step rests with New Delhi, and extradition under the bilateral treaty is itself a legal process. Why it matters: extradition treaty, India-Bangladesh ties.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• India-Bangladesh Extradition Treaty dates from 2013; MEA lists it among India's extradition treaties and arrangements. https://www.mea.gov.in/leta
• An amendment to the India-Bangladesh Extradition Treaty was signed in July 2016 during the Bangladesh Home Minister's visit. https://www.mea.gov.in/Uploads/PublicationDocs/29521_MEA_ANNUAL_REPORT_2016_17_new.pdf
• Treaty obliges each State to extradite persons charged with, found guilty of, or wanted to enforce a penalty for, an extraditable offence. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
• Extradition Act, 1962 is the legislative basis for extradition from India, which also needs a treaty, agreement or arrangement. https://www.mea.gov.in/extradition-from-india
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Treaty Article 6 lets a requested State refuse extradition if the offence is of a political character, so classification of the charges matters. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
• [Provision] The treaty duty to extradite is subject to its other provisions; refusal grounds are written into the text, so surrender is not automatic. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/BG13B1143.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Extradition Act, 1962 places no bar on extraditing Indian nationals, so India's own practice cuts both ways in any reciprocity argument. https://www.mea.gov.in/extradition-from-india
• [Example] The 2016 amendment shows the treaty can be revised by protocol when both governments agree, as during the July 2016 ministerial visit. https://www.mea.gov.in/Uploads/PublicationDocs/29521_MEA_ANNUAL_REPORT_2016_17_new.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] India-Bangladesh Extradition Treaty (2013): which refusal ground applies to offences of a political character? (Article 6; amended 2016).
[Mains 2027] Should India extradite Sheikh Hasina? Weigh the treaty's political-offence exception, bilateral ties and India's interests. (GS2, 15)
[Link] First appearance — no PYQ yet.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Disaster Management › Disaster and disaster management › Cyclones — IMD naming and warnings
CA Topic / Headline: Depression over the Bay of Bengal likely to become a very severe cyclonic storm, Cyclone Akvan, with gusts to 145 kmph; if it makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh it is the third cyclone in a month after Arnab and Murasu. Why it matters: IMD classes, naming, warnings.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• IMD classes: depression 31-49 kmph, deep depression 50-61, cyclonic storm 62-88, severe cyclonic storm 89-117 kmph. https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/sop.pdf
• Very severe cyclonic storm 64-89 knots, extremely severe 90-119 knots, super cyclonic storm 120 knots and above. https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/faq.pdf
• RSMC New Delhi names a North Indian Ocean cyclone once its maximum sustained wind reaches 34 knots (62 kmph). https://internal.imd.gov.in/press_release/20200428_pr_788.pdf
• Naming over the North Indian Ocean began in 2004 (first name Onil); names are used sequentially, column-wise. https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/Souvenir_RSMC_17Aug.pdf
• WMO/ESCAP Panel adopted a new name list in April 2020; it includes Arnab (Bangladesh), Murasu (India) and Akvan (Iran). https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/tc-names.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] IMD standard operating procedure links each cyclone class to expected damage and action, such as total suspension of fishing operations. https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/sop.pdf
• [Data] A cyclonic storm of 62-88 kmph causes damage to thatched huts and breaks tree branches; a severe storm extensively damages thatched roofs and power lines. https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/sop.pdf
• [Example] RSMC New Delhi names tropical cyclones forming over the North Indian Ocean, including the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea, from the agreed Panel list. https://internal.imd.gov.in/press_release/20200428_pr_788.pdf
• [Way forward] IMD FAQ: cyclone intensity and size are only weakly associated, so category alone does not show the area at risk; read warnings with track forecasts. https://rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in/images/pdf/faq.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] IMD classes a storm of 118-166 kmph as? (Very severe cyclonic storm; 64-89 knots). Akvan is a name contributed by which country? (Iran).
[Mains 2027] How are tropical cyclones named? Explain IMD's colour-coded warnings and the Fujiwhara effect on track and intensity. (GS1, 10)
[Link] Mains 2013 (naming), 2022 (colour-coded warnings), 2024 (sea surface temperature), 2026 (Fujiwhara); Prelims 2020 (cyclone eye); refined to Akvan.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Linkages between development and spread of extremism › LWE — National Policy and Action Plan 2015
CA Topic / Headline: PM Modi at Gadchiroli said Naxalism is over, citing a World Bank report on nearly 50 crore people out of extreme poverty and 125 affected districts in 2014; 246 projects worth ₹3,000 crore launched. Why it matters: LWE strategy, development-security link.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• National Policy and Action Plan to address LWE was approved in 2015: security measures, development interventions, rights and entitlements of local communities. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2026-pdfs/LS03022026/58.pdf
• Police and public order are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule; the Centre supplements State efforts against LWE. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2026-pdfs/LS03022026/58.pdf
• Security Related Expenditure (SRE) scheme reimburses LWE-affected States for operations, training, surrender-cum-rehabilitation and ex-gratia; ₹3,681.73 crore released since 2014-15. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2026-pdfs/LS03022026/58.pdf
• Special Central Assistance fills critical public-infrastructure gaps in Most LWE affected Districts; ₹3,953.67 crore released. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2223092&reg=3&lang=1
• Government set a deadline to eliminate Naxalism by 31 March 2026, termed Naxalmukt Bharat Abhiyan. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/apr/doc2025410538201.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] LWE violence incidents fell 89% from 1,936 in 2010 to 222 in 2025. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2025-pdfs/LS16122025/2591.pdf
• [Data] LWE-affected districts fell from 126 to 90 in April 2018, then 70 in July 2021; PIB now says no district is categorised as LWE affected. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2291043&reg=48&lang=1
• [Provision] Strategy is whole-of-government: security forces, India Reserve Battalions, helicopters, fortified police stations, intelligence sharing and State police modernisation funds. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2026-pdfs/LS03022026/481.pdf
• [Example] Surrender-cum-Rehabilitation Policy under SRE gives surrendered cadre an immediate grant and incentives for surrendering weapons and ammunition. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2223092&reg=3&lang=1
• [Way forward] Government says focus on development in tribal and remote areas addressed the root cause; sustain roads, schooling and entitlements in formerly affected districts. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2025-pdfs/RS17122025/1994.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] The National Policy and Action Plan to address LWE was approved in which year? (2015). Which scheme reimburses States for operations and surrenders? (SRE).
[Mains 2027] LWE was to be eliminated by March 2026: explain LWE and the measures taken, and the way forward for formerly affected districts. (GS3, 10)
[Link] Mains 2018, 2022, 2025 (LWE approach, strategy, 2026 deadline); entry refined to the Gadchiroli claim of Naxalism ending.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › NGT Act 2010 — polluter pays and restitution
CA Topic / Headline: Supreme Court set aside the NGT's December 2017 order holding the Art of Living's World Culture Festival liable for Yamuna floodplain damage; the ₹5 crore deposited as environmental compensation is to be refunded. Why it matters: polluter pays, NGT Act 2010 sections 15 and 20.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NGT was established under Section 3 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 (Act 19 of 2010), in force from 18 October 2010. https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/sites/default/files/rti_gazette_notification/Information_Relating_To_National_Green_Tribunal_Under_Section_4(1)_(B)_of_The_Right_To_Information_Act_2005.pdf
• Section 15(1): relief and compensation to victims of pollution under Schedule I enactments, restitution of damaged property, and restitution of the environment. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2025/1/AA2010__19green.pdf
• Section 20: while passing orders the NGT must apply sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle. https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/sites/default/files/rti_gazette_notification/Information_Relating_To_National_Green_Tribunal_Under_Section_4(1)_(B)_of_The_Right_To_Information_Act_2005.pdf
• Section 14 gives original jurisdiction over substantial environmental questions; Section 16 gives appellate jurisdiction against specified orders. https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/sites/default/files/news_updates/Rejoinder%20of%20the%20Applicant%20to%20Reply%20filed%20by%20R-2%20in%20OA%20No.89-2020%20(page%20nos.573-666).pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] NGT Principal Bench: under polluter pays, the polluter bears restoration cost; environmental compensation funds remediation, as part of sustainable development. https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/gen_pdf_test.php?filepath=L25ndF9kb2N1bWVudHMvbmd0L2Nhc2Vkb2MvanVkZ2VtZW50cy9ERUxISS8yMDIzLTEyLTA3LzE3MDE5NDI5MzM0OTk0OTU2ODY2NTcxOTY5NTA1NTc4LnBkZg%3D%3D
• [Provision] Section 15(1)(a) compensation is tied to Schedule I enactments; restitution of property and environment under (b) and (c) carries no such wording. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2025/1/AA2010__19green.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Limitation can bar claims: Section 14 disputes carry a six-month period, and Section 15 relief claims must be filed within five years. https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/sites/default/files/news_updates/Compilation%20of%20Case%20Law%20by%20Applicant%20in%20OA%20No.35-2022%20(page%20nos.444-520).pdf
• [Provision] Article 21 includes the right to a clean and healthy environment; no person has a legal or fundamental right to pollute it. https://www.greentribunal.gov.in/gen_pdf_test.php?filepath=L25ndF9kb2N1bWVudHMvbmd0L2Nhc2Vkb2MvanVkZ2VtZW50cy9ERUxISS8yMDIzLTEyLTA3LzE3MDE5NDI5MzM0OTk0OTU2ODY2NTcxOTY5NTA1NTc4LnBkZg%3D%3D
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] How does the NGT differ from the CPCB? Which principles must the NGT apply under section 20 of the 2010 Act?
[Mains 2027] Polluter pays presupposes a polluter: evaluate the NGT's compensation power in light of the Supreme Court's festival ruling. (GS3, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2018 (NGT vs CPCB), 2012 (NGT Act and Article 21); entry refined to the Yamuna floodplain ruling.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Constitution: historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions, basic structure › Freedom of religion — Articles 25 and 26
CA Topic / Headline: Tamil Nadu told the Supreme Court no established practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp on the Thirupparankundram hill exists and no right under Articles 25-26 was pleaded or proved. Why it matters: essential religious practice, denominational rights, State control of temples.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 25(1): all persons equally entitled to freedom of conscience and to freely profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/19150/1/constitution_of_india.pdf
• Article 25(2) preserves State power to regulate economic, financial, political or other secular activity associated with religious practice. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2006/9287/9287_2006_1_1501_57054_Judgement_08-Nov-2024.pdf
• Article 26: every religious denomination or section may establish institutions, manage its own religious affairs, own property and administer it in accordance with law. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-26-freedom-to-manage-religious-affairs/
• Articles 25 to 28 fall under the heading Right to freedom of religion; Article 25 protects persons, Article 26 denominations and sections. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2006/9287/9287_2006_1_1501_57054_Judgement_08-Nov-2024.pdf
• Supreme Court: Article 25 protects the right to transmit or spread religion by exposition of its tenets; it gives no right to convert others. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/5403.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] Courts may decide whether a rite is essential to a religion; the Tandava dance case tested it under Articles 25 and 26. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/9690.pdf
• [Judgment] A religious denomination has the right to manage its own religious affairs, including spending trust property on religious purposes set by the founder. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/949.pdf
• [Judgment] Auroville case: Shri Aurobindo's teachings were held not religious, so the Society and township were not a religious denomination under Articles 25 and 26. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/9868.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Article 26 rights are subject to public order, morality and health, and Article 26(d) allows administering property only in accordance with law. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-26-freedom-to-manage-religious-affairs/
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Article 26 grants which right to a religious denomination? (to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, subject to public order, morality, health).
[Mains 2027] How does Indian secularism differ from the Western model? Discuss with the Article 25-26 limits on religious practice. (GS1, 10)
[Link] Mains 2014, 2018, 2019 (secularism, cultural practices); no direct PYQ on Articles 25-26 text; entry refined to Thirupparankundram.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › Student suicides — UGC equity regulations and National Task Force
CA Topic / Headline: The National Task Force set up by the Supreme Court in 2025 found 2,473 complaints under UGC's 2012 Equity Regulations, 2,430 resolved and 43 pending; 10 States reported none; it calls the Equal Opportunity Cell among the most neglected bodies. Why it matters: student mental health, campus discrimination.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2012 apply to all higher educational institutions in India. https://www.ugc.gov.in/pdfnews/4360105_UGC-Promotion-of-Equity-in-Higher-Educational-Institutions-Regulations-2012.pdf
• The Regulations target discrimination on caste, creed, religion, language, ethnicity, gender and disabilities; equity means a level playing field for all students. https://www.ugc.gov.in/pdfnews/4360105_UGC-Promotion-of-Equity-in-Higher-Educational-Institutions-Regulations-2012.pdf
• The Regulations provide for Equal Opportunity Cells in each higher educational institution. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1577808&reg=48&lang=2
• UGC gives financial assistance to eligible colleges and universities to set up Equal Opportunity Centres for disadvantaged groups. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1577808&reg=48&lang=2
• Supreme Court constituted a National Task Force, headed by a former Supreme Court judge, on student mental well-being in higher educational institutions. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/30988/30988_2019_3_10_61151_Order_24-Apr-2025.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] UGC mechanisms against caste discrimination: Equal Opportunity Cells, SC/ST grievance redressal committees and liaison officers for SC/ST students and staff. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2197829&reg=3&lang=1
• [Judgment] Supreme Court order of 24 April 2025: aims at an institutional mechanism for student well-being against suicides from discrimination, academic pressure and harassment. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/30988/30988_2019_3_10_61151_Order_24-Apr-2025.pdf
• [Judgment] 2026 INSC 62: the Task Force reviewed laws, policies and public data on student suicides from SRS and NCRB sources. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/40105/40105_2024_7_301_67552_Judgement_15-Jan-2026.pdf
• [Example] The Court declined to restrain notification of draft UGC Equity Regulations, 2025, noting they are in the right direction on preventing on-campus discrimination. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/30988/30988_2019_3_10_61151_Order_24-Apr-2025.pdf
• [Way forward] Build support systems that ameliorate, not exacerbate, existing inequities, to disarm stressors that fall hardest on marginalised students. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2024/40105/40105_2024_7_301_67552_Judgement_15-Jan-2026.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2012 require which body in every institution? (Equal Opportunity Cell).
[Mains 2027] Student suicides in higher education: assess the UGC equity framework and the National Task Force's case for institutional support systems. (GS2, 15)
[Link] First appearance — no PYQ yet.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › Health financing — National Health Accounts and OOPE
CA Topic / Headline: Union government health spending more than tripled to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-24 from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-14; household out-of-pocket share fell 21.5 percentage points, per the latest National Health Accounts estimates. Why it matters: UHC, health financing.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NHA 2022-23 is the tenth report, prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat at NHSRC, using the System of Health Accounts 2011 framework. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2265816&reg=1&lang=1
• Government Health Expenditure share of Total Health Expenditure rose from 28.6% (2013-14) to 43.7% (2022-23). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2265816&reg=1&lang=1
• Out-of-pocket expenditure share of Total Health Expenditure fell from 64.2% in 2013-14 to 43.4% in 2022-23. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2265816&reg=1&lang=1
• WHO Global Health Expenditure Database offers comparable health expenditure data for 195 countries and territories since 2000. https://apps.who.int/nha/database/
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Decade trend: rising government spending cut the households' out-of-pocket share from 64.2% to 43.4% of total health expenditure by 2022-23. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2265816&reg=1&lang=1
• [Counterpoint] WHO 2024: out-of-pocket spending stayed the main health financing source in 30 low and lower-middle-income countries. https://www.who.int/news/item/12-12-2024-new-who-report-reveals-governments-deprioritizing-health-spending
• [Data] WHO: average per capita government health spending fell in 2022 from 2021 in all income groups after the early pandemic surge. https://www.who.int/news/item/12-12-2024-new-who-report-reveals-governments-deprioritizing-health-spending
• [Way forward] Protecting people from financial hardship due to out-of-pocket health costs is fundamental to health for all, WHO says on UHC Day. https://www.who.int/news/item/12-12-2024-new-who-report-reveals-governments-deprioritizing-health-spending
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] In National Health Accounts, which share rose from 28.6% in 2013-14 to 43.7% in 2022-23? (Government Health Expenditure in Total Health Expenditure).
[Mains 2027] Out-of-pocket spending is still large despite rising public health spending: evaluate India's health financing trends and the way forward. (GS2, 15)
[Link] First appearance — no PYQ yet.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Indian economy: planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, development and employment › Monetary policy — MPC and inflation targeting
CA Topic / Headline: Headline CPI inflation was 6.09% in October 2026, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit; food inflation 8.94%; the MPC raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50%. Why it matters: inflation targeting, Section 45ZN, food inflation.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 45ZA, RBI Act 1934: Centre, with RBI, fixes the inflation target; 2016 notification set 4%, upper tolerance 6%, lower 2%. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?relid=151264&reg=48&lang=2
• MPC has six members: three from RBI including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, and three appointed by the Centre on a Search-cum-Selection Committee's recommendation. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=148405&reg=48&lang=2
• MPC fixes the benchmark policy rate (repo rate) needed to contain inflation within the target; provisions came into force on 27 June 2016. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?relid=151264&reg=48&lang=2
• MPC must meet at least four times a year; failure to meet the target is examined under Section 45ZN. https://prsindia.org/theprsblog/inflation-targets-not-met-%E2%80%93-mpc-to-examine-today
• Centre sets the CPI inflation target every five years with RBI; 4% with ±2% band notified in 2016, retained in March 2021. https://prsindia.org/policy/monthly-policy-review/august-2025
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The statutory framework makes price stability the objective while keeping in mind growth; the MPC uses the repo rate as its instrument. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?relid=151264&reg=48&lang=2
• [Provision] Failure to meet the target triggers Section 45ZN scrutiny; factors constituting failure were notified in the Gazette on 27 June 2016. https://prsindia.org/theprsblog/inflation-targets-not-met-%E2%80%93-mpc-to-examine-today
• [Provision] Inflation outside the tolerance band for three consecutive quarters is considered a failure under the flexible inflation-targeting framework. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/review-of-monetary-policy-framework-by-rbi
• [Data] Average inflation fell from 6.8% in 2012-16 to 4.9% since the framework began; headline stayed within 2-6% three-fourths of the time in the first review period. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/review-of-monetary-policy-framework-by-rbi
• [Counterpoint] Arguments exist to drop food and fuel from the target as they are volatile and respond weakly to monetary policy; all targeters except Uganda use headline inflation. https://prsindia.org/policy/report-summaries/review-of-monetary-policy-framework-by-rbi
• [Way forward] A review of the inflation target was due by the end of March 2026, so band width and the headline-versus-core choice remain open. https://prsindia.org/policy/monthly-policy-review/august-2025
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] MPC has six members, three from RBI, with the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson: which statements are correct? (target 4% within a 2-6% band).
[Mains 2027] Causes of persistent food inflation and effectiveness of RBI monetary policy against it. (GS3, 10)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Security forces and agencies and their mandate › Coastal security — Sea Vigil and CDSRE
CA Topic / Headline: Indian Navy's Sea Vigil-26, the fifth Pan-India Coastal Defence Exercise, runs 11-19 Nov: CDSRE audit phase, then Sea Phase with Red and Blue forces; conceptualised in 2018 after 26/11. Why it matters: maritime security architecture.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Sea Vigil-26, fifth edition of the Pan-India Coastal Defence Exercise, runs 11-19 November 2026 with the Indian Navy as lead agency. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2335093&reg=48&lang=2
• Phases: Coastal Defence and Security Readiness Evaluation (CDSRE) 11-17 November, then the Sea Phase on 18-19 November 2026. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2335093&reg=48&lang=2
• Sea Vigil was conceptualised in 2018 to validate maritime security measures after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks; first held 22-23 January 2019. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1570836
• Sea Vigil-26 spans the entire coastline and Exclusive Economic Zone and involves all Coastal States and Union Territories. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2335093&reg=48&lang=2
• The drill is a build-up to the Navy's Theatre Level Readiness Operational Exercise (TROPEX). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2335415&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Sea Vigil 24 CDSRE audited over 950 critical coastal locations including fish landing centres, lighthouses, ports and coastal police stations. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2076147
• [Provision] Sea Vigil 24 spanned the 11,098 km coastline and involved six Central ministries and 21 Central and State agencies. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2075105&reg=3&lang=2
• [Example] Sea Vigil 24 served as a platform to evaluate inter-agency coordination and identify gaps in India's coastal security infrastructure. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2076147
• [Way forward] Sea Vigil is a national-level initiative giving a holistic appraisal of maritime defence capability beyond State exercises; follow up on the gaps it identifies. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2073000
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Sea Vigil was conceptualised to validate maritime security measures after which event? (26/11 Mumbai attacks; first held January 2019).
[Mains 2027] What are India's maritime security challenges? Discuss organisational, technical and procedural initiatives, including Sea Vigil. (GS3, 10)
[Link] Mains 2022 (maritime security challenges); entry refined to Sea Vigil-26.

[Prelims 2027] Census 2027 is the 16th Census of India; its reference date is 00:00 hours of which day? (1 March 2027).
