Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › Great Nicobar project — ICTP Galathea Bay, FRA and Shompen
CA Topic / Headline: A tender for boundary pillars of the Great Nicobar project was made public on October 26, a month before the Calcutta High Court's final hearing (November 25-26) on challenges to its forest clearance over alleged Forest Rights Act violations. Why it matters: development vs ecology and tribal rights.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Project components: 14.2 million TEU transhipment terminal, greenfield airport (4,000 peak-hour passengers), 450 MVA gas-solar plant and a township. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?NoteId=158406&ModuleId=3&reg=3&lang=1
• Galathea Bay port lies about 40 nautical miles from the East-West shipping route, with natural depth over 20 metres. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2257174&reg=48&lang=2
• The proposed township spans 16,610 hectares. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/may/doc202651860401.pdf
• ICTP project cost was put at ₹44,313 crore in PM GatiShakti Network Planning Group evaluation. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2047614&reg=48&lang=2
• ICTP is a key project under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1979157&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Government says no displacement is proposed for Shompen and Nicobarese and notified tribal reserve area will rise through re-notification. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/may/doc202654862601.pdf
• [Data] The project aims to reduce dependence on foreign transhipment ports and serve defence and national security purposes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?NoteId=158406&ModuleId=3&reg=3&lang=1
• [Example] Government FAQ: project strengthens India's presence in the Andaman Sea and Southeast Asia and integrates the island with global trade. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/may/doc202651861901.pdf
• [Way forward] Government FAQ says PVTGs, especially Shompen, must not be adversely affected; FRA consent processes need verifiable compliance. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/may/doc202651861901.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] The International Container Transhipment Port of the Great Nicobar project is planned at which bay? (Galathea Bay).
[Mains 2027] The Great Nicobar project pits strategic and economic gains against ecological and tribal concerns. Critically examine. (GS3, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2017 (Great Nicobar geography); refined to boundary-pillar tender and FRA challenge.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Economy › Indian economy: planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, development and employment › Core industries — Index of Eight Core Industries 2022-23 series
CA Topic / Headline: Core sector growth hit a series-high 10.9% in October 2026, led by coal and electricity (21.6%), with cement at 15.4% and iron ore at 23.4%; a low base of 0.8% last October aided the figure. Why it matters: industrial output, ICI methodology.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The new ICI series has base year 2022-23; weights derive from the IIP (2022-23) and are scaled to 100. https://eaindustry.nic.in/uploaded_files/ici/ICI_FAQS.pdf
• Electricity weight rose from 19.853% to 30.932% in the 2022-23 ICI series. https://eaindustry.nic.in/uploaded_files/ici/ICI_FAQS.pdf
• Iron ore was added to the ICI basket in the 2022-23 series with a 4.905% weight. https://eaindustry.nic.in/uploaded_files/ici/ICI_FAQS.pdf
• In the 2011-12 series, refinery products had the highest weight at 28.04%. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1920543
• In the 2011-12 series, eight core industries were 40.27% of IIP item weights. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1920543
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Only raw coal is retained in the new ICI series; coal middlings and washed coal are dropped to avoid double counting. https://eaindustry.nic.in/uploaded_files/ici/ICI_FAQS.pdf
• [Data] Electricity weight rose due to higher GVA of the sector from 2011-12 to 2022-23 and inclusion of renewable sources. https://eaindustry.nic.in/uploaded_files/ici/ICI_FAQS.pdf
• [Example] First press release of the 2022-23 ICI series gives refinery products 22.572 and steel 17.584 weights. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2286615&reg=48&lang=1
• [Counterpoint] ICI measures production of eight core industries only, so a low base or one sector can drive headline growth. https://eaindustry.nic.in/eight_core_infra/eight_infra.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] In the new ICI (2022-23) series, which sector has the highest weight? (Electricity, about 30.9%).
[Mains 2027] What does the Index of Core Industries reveal about industrial momentum? Discuss its new 2022-23 series and limits as a lead indicator. (GS3, 10)
[Link] Prelims 2015 (highest weight in ICI), 2012 (core industries list); refined to 2022-23 series and record October growth.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Separation of powers between organs; dispute redressal mechanisms and institutions › Inter-State water disputes — Cauvery, Mekedatu
CA Topic / Headline: Supreme Court dismissed Tamil Nadu's plea that Karnataka make good a shortfall of 16.01 tmc ft (later 11.719 tmc ft) of Cauvery water pro rata in 2026-27; Karnataka said the ruling curbs States rushing to court against the expert CWMA. Why it matters: water federalism.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Parliament enacted the ISRWD Act, 1956 under Article 262; it was last amended in August 2002. https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/05/2023022017.pdf
• Cauvery Water Management Scheme was notified on 1 June 2018, constituting CWMA and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee. https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/05/2023022017.pdf
• SC (February 2018) cut Karnataka's normal-year delivery to Tamil Nadu at Biligundlu from 192 TMC to 177.25 TMC. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1736883&reg=3&lang=2
• Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted on 2 June 1990. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/12741.pdf
• A Tribunal decision, once published, has the same force as an order or decree of the Supreme Court (Section 6(2)). https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=93648&reg=3&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Article 262 lets Parliament bar the Supreme Court and other courts from inter-State river water disputes. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/12741.pdf
• [Judgment] The CWDT award merged with the SC judgment of 16 February 2018, and the CWDT was dissolved. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1542169&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] In 2023 the SC declined to interfere with CWRC and CWMA release orders, noting they consist of water and agriculture experts. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/44880/44880_2018_4_101_47113_Order_21-Sep-2023.pdf
• [Way forward] CWMA has powers over storage, apportionment and regulation to secure compliance with the modified award; States should use it before courts. https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/05/997297f54ac7a907ad664389b81e5b5e.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under which section of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 was the Cauvery Water Management Authority constituted? (Section 6A).
[Mains 2027] Do expert bodies like the Cauvery Water Management Authority reduce litigation in inter-State water disputes? Examine. (GS2, 10)
[Link] Mains 2013 (mechanisms for water disputes); Essay 2016 (water disputes in federal India); refined to SC dismissal of TN shortfall plea.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Functions and responsibilities of Union and States; federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels › Delimitation — Article 82, seat freeze, Census
CA Topic / Headline: Congress proposed a four-point formula for delimitation, retaining the Lok Sabha's 543 seats and reserving one-third for women, and said the INDIA bloc was on board. Why it matters: federal balance, seat freeze, women's reservation.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• 42nd Amendment (1976) froze each State's Lok Sabha and Assembly seats on the 1971 census until the first census after 2000. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-delimitation-bill-2026
• 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze until the first census after 2026. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-delimitation-bill-2026
• The last Delimitation Commission was set up in 2002 and its orders were finalised in 2008. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/issues-for-consideration-1776322954
• The 2002 Commission, chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh, began functioning on 4 July 2002. https://www.eci.gov.in/eci-backend/public/all_files/delimitation/Procedure(English).pdf
• Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 16 April 2026. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-bill-summary-1776322465
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Under Article 82, Parliament enacts a Delimitation Act after every census; the Centre then constitutes a Delimitation Commission. https://old.eci.gov.in/faqs/elections/delimitation-of-constituencies/faqs-delimitation-of-constituencies-r6/
• [Provision] Delimitation Bill, 2026 uses the latest published census when the Commission is constituted, implying the 2011 census. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-delimitation-bill-2026
• [Data] Home Minister: with seats frozen since 1971, 127 constituencies have more than 20 lakh voters each. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253186&reg=3&lang=1
• [Counterpoint] The 2001 freeze was a motivational measure so States could pursue population stabilisation; population-only seats could penalise them. https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/879abe65ba0eac1dbfffa83ba5cd0438.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which Constitutional Amendment extended the freeze on Lok Sabha seat allocation till the first census after 2026? (84th Amendment, 2001).
[Mains 2027] Delimitation must balance equal representation with federal fairness. Evaluate alternatives to population-only seat allocation. (GS2, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2012 (Delimitation Commission orders), 2024 (number of commissions); Mains 2026 (women's representation); refines 13 Nov entry.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › Maternal health — caesarean deliveries in private hospitals
CA Topic / Headline: Plum Data Labs analysis of over 1,60,000 delivery-related insurance claims shows the average C-section rate among insured births in private hospitals at an all-time high of 69%; four cities with the lowest rates are in Tamil Nadu. Why it matters: over-medicalisation, OOPE, regulation.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• WHO (April 2015): population-level C-section rates above 10% are not associated with lower maternal and newborn mortality. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=177374&reg=48&lang=2
• About 15% of pregnancies are assumed to develop complications requiring surgical intervention. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=177374&reg=48&lang=2
• Institutional births rose from 79% (NFHS-4) to 89% (NFHS-5). https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1843842&reg=48&lang=2
• NFHS-6 (2023-24): institutional deliveries rose from 88.6% to 90.6%. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2266600&reg=3&lang=1
• NFHS-4 Delhi: C-sections were 42.9% of births in private facilities versus 21% in public ones. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=177374&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] IIT Madras study: private-sector C-section share rose from 43.1% (2016) to 49.7% (2021), nearly one in two deliveries. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2016771&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] IIT Madras found place of delivery mattered most, implying clinical need was not necessarily the reason for surgical deliveries. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2016771&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] NFHS-5 recorded a substantial rise in C-section deliveries in many States, especially in private facilities. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1774533&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Caesarean section is life-saving when needed but carries inherent surgical risks; audit private-sector rates against clinical indications. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=177374&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Per WHO (2015), C-section rates above what level are not linked to lower maternal and newborn mortality at population level? (10%).
[Mains 2027] Rising caesarean deliveries in private hospitals point to supply-induced demand. Suggest regulatory and insurance reforms. (GS2, 10)
[Link] first appearance — no PYQ yet

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Parliament and State legislatures: structure, functioning, conduct of business, powers and privileges › FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 — JPC consultation
CA Topic / Headline: Opposition members forced the parliamentary panel scrutinising the FCRA Amendment Bill to defer its meeting with officials, saying stakeholders who sought to depose had not been heard; the Bill would vest assets of cancelled registrations in a designated authority. Why it matters: NGO regulation, committee scrutiny.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• FCRA 2010 replaced the 1976 Act; Presidential assent was on 26 September 2010. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/jul/doc2026722929001.pdf
• 2020 amendment: foreign contribution only in an 'FCRA account' at State Bank of India, New Delhi Main Branch; sub-granting to other associations prohibited. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2287897&reg=48&lang=2
• 2020 amendment cut the administrative expense ceiling from 50% to 20% of foreign contribution received. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-foreign-contribution-regulation-amendment-bill-2020
• Registration ceases after five years unless renewed; the 2020 amendment requires Aadhaar or passport details of office-bearers. https://fcraonline.nic.in/home/PDF_Doc/fc_faq_04102022.pdf
• Suspension of registration is up to 180 days, extendable by a further 180 days after the 2020 amendment. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-foreign-contribution-regulation-amendment-bill-2020
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Centre cancelled over 19,000 recipient registrations between 2011 and 2019, the Statement of Objects of the 2020 Bill recorded. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2020/FCRA%20Amendment%202020.pdf
• [Provision] Section 3 bars foreign contribution to election candidates and others, and to acceptance that harms sovereignty, integrity, security or communal harmony. https://fcraonline.nic.in/home/PDF_Doc/fc_faq_04102022.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Government says FCRA is a transparency and disclosure framework, not a ban: receipts must be registered, channelled through a designated account and reported. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2287897&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] Nearly 20,000 cancelled registrations and about 15,000 deemed ceased left thousands of crore of assets in limbo under Section 15 vesting. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2287897&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] Provide a clear State authority to take possession of assets of cancelled registrations and ensure proportionate, hearing-based cancellation. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2287897&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under the FCRA, which Ministry administers registration of organisations receiving foreign contribution? (Ministry of Home Affairs).
[Mains 2027] Does tighter foreign-funding regulation strengthen accountability or shrink civic space? Examine the FCRA Amendment Bill and committee scrutiny. (GS2, 10)
[Link] Mains 2015 (NGO foreign funding); refines the 14 Nov entry on JPC consultation.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Role of external state and non-state actors in internal security challenges › Mutual legal assistance — MLATs and letters rogatory
CA Topic / Headline: NIA sent a mutual legal assistance request to the UAE in its probe into a flydubai co-pilot, seeking evidence under the MLAT framework alongside letters rogatory and extradition channels. Why it matters: cross-border investigation, international cooperation.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• MHA is the nodal Ministry and Central Authority for seeking and giving mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. https://www.mea.gov.in/mutual-legal-assistance-in-criminal-matters
• MHA's IS-II Division handles mutual legal assistance in criminal matters. https://www.mea.gov.in/cpv-mlat-menu
• Section 105 CrPC provides for reciprocal arrangements with foreign governments on service of summons and judicial processes. https://www.mea.gov.in/mutual-legal-assistance-in-criminal-matters
• India had MLATs or agreements with 42 countries and is party to UNCAC and UNTOC (2020). https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1598852&reg=3&lang=2
• MHA's International Cooperation Division negotiates MLATs and security cooperation agreements. https://www.mha.gov.in/en/commoncontent/international-cooperation-division
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Assistance is sought through MLA requests, letters rogatory, and service of summons on persons residing abroad. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1598852
• [Example] India-US MLAT requires assistance whether or not the conduct is an offence under the requested State's law. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/LegalTreatiesDoc/US01B0634-1-1.pdf
• [Data] MHA guidelines set service of documents abroad preferably within 10 days for offences against women and children. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1598852
• [Way forward] MHA runs mutual legal assistance training for investigators, prosecutors and judicial officers; expand it to cut delays. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1598852
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which Ministry is India's Central Authority for mutual legal assistance in criminal matters? (Ministry of Home Affairs).
[Mains 2027] Cross-border investigations depend on MLATs and letters rogatory. Examine the hurdles India faces and suggest reforms. (GS3, 10)
[Link] first appearance — no PYQ yet

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › Cosmetics safety — heavy metals and Cosmetics Rules 2020
CA Topic / Headline: Fairness creams with heavy metals are emerging as a health hazard: a 17-year-old in Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a cream bought online after influencer promotion; Keralam launched a campaign against spurious cosmetics. Why it matters: drug-cosmetic regulation, online sales.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Cosmetics are regulated under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Cosmetics Rules, 2020. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/export/sites/CDSCO_WEB/Pdf-documents/cosmetics/Guidance-Document-on-Registration-and-Import-of-cosmetics-into-India-converted.pdf
• Cosmetics Rules, 2020 were notified by GSR 763(E) dated 15 December 2020. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/export/sites/CDSCO_WEB/Pdf-documents/cosmetics/Frequently-Asked-Questions-FAQcosmeticia.pdf
• State Licensing Authorities license cosmetic manufacture; the DCGI, as Central Licensing Authority, registers imports. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/opencms/en/Cosmetics/cosmetics/
• Drugs and Cosmetics Rules prohibit cosmetics containing mercury compounds and lead or arsenic compounds for colouring. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=103826&reg=48&lang=2
• BIS standards set maximum limits of 20 ppm for lead and 2 ppm for arsenic in cosmetics. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=103826&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Section 3(aaa) of the 1940 Act defines a cosmetic as an article applied to the body for cleansing, beautifying or altering appearance. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/export/sites/CDSCO_WEB/Pdf-documents/cosmetics/Guidancedoccos.pdf
• [Provision] Section 10 bars import of cosmetics that are not of standard quality, or are misbranded or spurious. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2022/acts_and_rules/Drugs%20and%20Cosmetics%20Act,%201940.pdf
• [Example] CDSCO lists heavy-metal test reports for mercury, lead and arsenic that do not meet Cosmetics Rules limits as a common non-compliance. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/export/sites/CDSCO_WEB/Pdf-documents/cosmetics/General-Non-compliances-Observed-converted.pdf
• [Way forward] Import registration requires a declaration on heavy metal and hexachlorophene content; extend similar scrutiny to products sold online. https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/export/sites/CDSCO_WEB/Pdf-documents/cosmetics/Guidancedoccos.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Who is the Central Licensing Authority for import registration of cosmetics in India? (Drugs Controller General of India).
[Mains 2027] Spurious cosmetics sold online and promoted by influencers pose a public-health risk. Assess India's cosmetics regulatory framework. (GS2, 10)
[Link] first appearance — no PYQ yet

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Important international institutions, agencies and fora: structure, mandate › IMO — net-zero framework for shipping
CA Topic / Headline: India is a swing vote at the coming IMO meeting on decarbonising global shipping; it has not decided its position, which will follow the principle of climate justice and CBDR-RC. In October 2025 the U.S. disrupted the IMO vote on the framework. Why it matters: green shipping, trade costs.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• India was re-elected to the IMO Council in Category B, the 10 States with the largest interest in seaborne trade, for 2026-27. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2196409&reg=3&lang=1
• India topped Category B with 154 of 169 valid votes at the 34th IMO Assembly on 28 November 2025. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2196103&reg=3&lang=2
• The IMO Council has 40 members: 10 each in Categories A and B and 20 in Category C. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1511825&reg=3&lang=2
• India has served on the IMO Council since it began functioning, except during 1983-1984. https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=131979&reg=48&lang=2
• India is a founder member of the IMO, the UN specialised agency on maritime safety and marine environment protection. https://shipmin.gov.in/sites/default/files/2017-18%20English.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India's Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines (2023) set a roadmap to cut carbon intensity at major ports. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/dec/doc20251215731201.pdf
• [Example] Green Tug Transition Programme (2024) and Harit Nauka initiative promote low-emission, alternative-fuel vessels. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2105085&reg=3&lang=2
• [Data] India has more than 145,000 active seafarers, giving it a large stake in global shipping rules. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1511825&reg=3&lang=2
• [Way forward] Minister: green hydrogen, ammonia, biofuels and LNG are the future of maritime fuels; India can supply green fuels to global shipping. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2105085&reg=3&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] The 2023 IMO GHG Strategy aims for net-zero emissions from international shipping by when? (By or around 2050).
[Mains 2027] Should India back a global carbon price on shipping under the IMO net-zero framework? Weigh climate justice against trade and green-fuel opportunities. (GS2, 15)
[Link] Mains 2023 (role of IMO); refined to India as swing vote on shipping decarbonisation.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Functions and responsibilities of Union and States; federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels › Ladakh hill councils — LAHDC polls and Sixth Schedule demand
CA Topic / Headline: Ladakh's first panchayat polls since it became a UT recorded 70.03% turnout and 52.4% in municipal council polls; the Leh Apex Body questioned the timing amid talks on Statehood and the Sixth Schedule, and some villages boycotted. Why it matters: local democracy in UTs.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2) and 275(1)) lists ten tribal areas: Assam 3, Meghalaya 3, Tripura 1, Mizoram 3, each an autonomous district. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-standing-committee-report-summary-3175
• A Sixth Schedule District Council has at most 30 members: up to four nominated by the Governor, the rest elected on adult suffrage. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/schedules/provisions-as-to-the-administration-of-tribal-areas-in-the-states-of-assam-meghalaya-tripura-and-mizoram/
• The Bardoloi Committee drafted the Sixth Schedule to protect tribal areas and customs while enabling their development. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2007/legis1223890886_The_Constitution__One_Hundred_and_Seventh_Amendment__Bill__2007_0.pdf
• Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council Act, 1997 (Act XXXI of 1997) provides for hill councils and an Inter-District Advisory Council. https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/5859?view_type=browse
• Leh's hill council began in 1995 on the Darjeeling pattern; Kargil's followed in July 2003. https://kargil.nic.in/lahdc/
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Sixth Schedule councils may levy land revenue and taxes and regulate money-lending and trading by non-tribals. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/schedules/provisions-as-to-the-administration-of-tribal-areas-in-the-states-of-assam-meghalaya-tripura-and-mizoram/
• [Committee] Ramachandran Committee recommended stating the minimum powers of District Councils in the Constitution, since devolved powers differ. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2007/legis1223890886_The_Constitution__One_Hundred_and_Seventh_Amendment__Bill__2007_0.pdf
• [Scheme] 125th Amendment Bill, 2019 proposed larger councils, village and municipal councils and wider law-making powers for Sixth Schedule councils. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/prs-products/prs-standing-committee-report-summary-3175
• [Counterpoint] Autonomy is conditional: council regulations need the Governor's approval, and the Governor may assume council functions if administration fails. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/schedules/provisions-as-to-the-administration-of-tribal-areas-in-the-states-of-assam-meghalaya-tripura-and-mizoram/
• [Way forward] Legislate minimum devolved powers and village and municipal tiers, as the 125th Amendment Bill proposed. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-constitution-one-hundred-and-twenty-fifth-amendment-bill-2019

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › Important international institutions, agencies and fora: structure, mandate › Lethal autonomous weapons — CCW talks
CA Topic / Headline: States at the UN Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons agreed to discussions aiming to regulate lethal autonomous weapons in two years; about 100 countries sought legally binding rules, but the U.S., Russia and Israel opposed, leaving a watered-down deal. Why it matters: AI in warfare, arms control.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The CCW was negotiated under UN auspices in 1979-1980 and rests on IHL principles such as proportionality and distinction. https://www.un.org/en/un-chronicle/role-united-nations-addressing-emerging-technologies-area-lethal-autonomous-weapons
• The first formal meeting of the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS was held in Geneva, 13-17 November 2017. https://www.un.org/en/un-chronicle/role-united-nations-addressing-emerging-technologies-area-lethal-autonomous-weapons
• India's Ambassador Amandeep Singh Gill chaired the GGE on LAWS in 2017-2018. https://documents.un.org/doc/undoc/gen/g18/323/29/pdf/g1832329.pdf
• The GGE adopts its report by consensus and submits it to the Meeting of High Contracting Parties to the CCW. https://documents.un.org/doc/undoc/gen/g18/323/29/pdf/g1832329.pdf
• The GGE on LAWS was established by Decision 1 of the Fifth CCW Review Conference. https://documents.un.org/doc/undoc/gen/g24/181/91/pdf/g2418191.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India addresses LAWS within the CCW framework, which balances military necessity with humanitarian considerations. https://www.mea.gov.in/images/India_working_paper_GGE_LAWS.pdf
• [Counterpoint] India holds that emerging technologies could, in general, improve compliance with international humanitarian law. https://www.mea.gov.in/images/India_working_paper_GGE_LAWS.pdf
• [Example] Several States told the UN Secretary-General that the GGE balances humanitarian concerns with legitimate self-defence interests. https://documents.un.org/doc/undoc/gen/n24/154/32/pdf/n2415432.pdf
• [Way forward] Many States see the CCW structure, which allows new protocols, as suited to address emerging weapons technologies. https://documents.un.org/doc/undoc/gen/n24/154/32/pdf/n2415432.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Talks on lethal autonomous weapons systems are held under which treaty framework? (Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons).
[Mains 2027] Should lethal autonomous weapons be regulated by a legally binding instrument? Discuss India's position and IHL concerns. (GS2, 10)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › International Relations › India and its neighbourhood relations › India-Nepal — PM Balen Shah's visit
CA Topic / Headline: Nepal PM Balen Shah, in office since March after his Rastriya Swatantra Party won elections, arrived on his first official visit; External Affairs Minister Jaishankar called on him ahead of talks with PM Modi at Hyderabad House. Why it matters: Neighbourhood First, open border, connectivity.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Movement across the India-Nepal border is governed by the Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950, which allows free movement of citizens. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1497267&reg=3&lang=2
• Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is the border guarding force on the India-Nepal border. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1497267&reg=3&lang=2
• Nepal borders five Indian States: Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Open-bilateral-brief-20-June-2024.pdf
• About 32,000 Gorkha soldiers from Nepal serve in the Indian Army. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Open-bilateral-brief-20-June-2024.pdf
• India and Nepal signed a Treaty of Trade and Commerce at Kathmandu on 31 July 1950. https://mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F6291%2FTreaty+of+Trade+and+Commerce=
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] India is Nepal's largest trade partner; bilateral trade crossed USD 7 billion in 2019-20, and India transits almost all Nepal's third-country trade. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Nepal_2022.pdf
• [Example] India handed over 50,000 reconstructed houses in Gorkha and Nuwakot districts on 15 November 2021 (USD 150 million aid). https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Nepal_2022.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Demarcation of Kalapani and Susta is incomplete; Kalapani decides the India-Nepal-China tri-junction. https://mea.gov.in/distinguished-lectures-detail?674=
• [Way forward] Use the more than 40 bilateral mechanisms, including the Joint Commission, on border, power, water and railways. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Nepal-000doc.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Free movement of citizens across the India-Nepal border is governed by which treaty? (Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950).
[Mains 2027] India-Nepal ties rest on an open border and deep people-to-people links. Discuss the opportunities and irritants facing the relationship. (GS2, 15)
[Link] Prelims 2025 (BIMSTEC), 2026 (cross-border bridges); refined to Nepal PM's first visit.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Security challenges in border areas; organised crime and terrorism › India-China LAC — Corps Commander talks, Arunachal sector
CA Topic / Headline: India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks, which began on November 8 and ran nearly 10 days, to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh and prevent friction between troops before winter. Why it matters: border management, CBMs.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• India and China agreed in 2003 to appoint Special Representatives on the boundary question; 24 rounds held by August 2025. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-china-072026.pdf
• WMCC was set up by an agreement signed at the 15th round of SR talks, New Delhi, January 2012. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Bilateral-Brief-Updated_21-August-2023.pdf
• A 2005 protocol set modalities for confidence building measures along the LAC. https://mea.gov.in/Speeches-Statements.htm?dtl%2F38665%2FStatement_by_External_Affairs_Minister_Dr_S_Jaishankar_in_Lok_Sabha=
• India and China agreed on patrolling arrangements in Depsang and Demchok on 21 October 2024, leading to disengagement. https://mea.gov.in/lok-sabha.htm?dtl%2F38638%2FQUESTION+NO+714+RESTRICTIONS+ON+INDIAN+PATROLLING+IN+LADAKH=

Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] There is no commonly delineated LAC; differing perceptions lead to transgressions when both sides patrol up to their claims. https://www.mea.gov.in/images/pdf/RTI-12-08-2024.pdf
• [Data] Defence Ministry: in 2025 PLA kept 10 Combined Arms Brigade-size forces opposite the Northern borders. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210154&amp=&reg=3&amp=&lang=2
• [Example] Transgressions are taken up via border personnel meetings, flag meetings, WMCC and diplomatic channels. https://www.mea.gov.in/images/pdf/RTI-12-08-2024.pdf
• [Way forward] Both sides agreed to pursue disengagement, de-escalation, border management and eventual delimitation through existing mechanisms. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210154&amp=&reg=3&amp=&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] The Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) was set up in which year? (2012).
[Mains 2027] Despite multiple mechanisms, friction persists along the India-China LAC. Evaluate the border management architecture and suggest improvements. (GS3, 15)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Environment › Conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment › COP31 — fossil fuel transition and India's NDC
CA Topic / Headline: COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye ended without consensus after a record 48 hours of overtime; over 130 parties, led by the EU, rejected the cover text for omitting fossil fuels, while India, China and Saudi Arabia supported it. India said ambition must match means of implementation. Why it matters: climate multilateralism.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Updated NDC (August 2022): cut emissions intensity of GDP 45% by 2030 from 2005 level. https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/NDC/2022-08/India%20Updated%20First%20Nationally%20Determined%20Contrib.pdf
• NDC also targets about 50% cumulative installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1847813&reg=3&lang=2
• India's Panchamrit pledges at COP26, Glasgow included net-zero emissions by 2070. https://moef.gov.in/uploads/2022/11/Indias-LT-LEDS.pdf
• India submitted its first NDC on 2 October 2015. https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/NDC/2022-08/India%20Updated%20First%20Nationally%20Determined%20Contrib.pdf
• COP28 in Dubai (30 November-13 December 2023) adopted the outcome of the first Global Stocktake. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989495&reg=48&lang=2
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India adheres to Equity and Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) under UNFCCC. https://netzeroindia.moef.gov.in/about
• [Data] By June 2025 India had reduced emissions intensity of GDP by around 36% from 2005. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2249751&reg=3&lang=1
• [Example] India's NDC includes the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) mass movement as key to combating climate change. https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/NDC/2022-08/India%20Updated%20First%20Nationally%20Determined%20Contrib.pdf
• [Way forward] India links its 50% non-fossil target to technology transfer and low-cost international finance, including from the Green Climate Fund. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1885731&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under its updated NDC, India targets what share of installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030? (About 50%).

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, intellectual property rights › India-France space cooperation — TRISHNA
CA Topic / Headline: Op-ed on over 60 years of India-France space ties highlights TRISHNA, a joint ISRO-CNES thermal infrared mission: France supplies the thermal instrument and India the platform and an optical sensor; ISRO's chairman attended an International Space Summit in Paris in September 2026. Why it matters: water, agriculture, climate data.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• TRISHNA (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural resource Assessment) is a joint ISRO-CNES mission. https://www.isro.gov.in/TRISHNA_Mission.html
• CNES provides TRISHNA's thermal infrared payload, a four-channel long-wave infrared imaging sensor. https://www.isro.gov.in/TRISHNA_Mission.html
• TRISHNA will offer 60 m spatial resolution with a 3-day revisit at the equator, for 5 years with a possible 2-year extension. https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/pdf/Highlights/Flyer_Trishna_Workshop300724.pdf
• Joint ISRO-CNES satellites Megha-Tropiques and SARAL were launched on PSLV-C18 (2011) and PSLV-C20 (2013). https://www.isro.gov.in/france-and-italy.html
• Megha-Tropiques studies the water cycle in the tropical atmosphere; the ISRO-CNES MoU was signed in May 2001. https://archive.pib.gov.in/archive/releases98/lyr2001/rmay2001/10052001/r100520013.html
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] India-France Joint Vision for Space Cooperation (March 2018) covers climate monitoring, TRISHNA and space situational awareness. https://mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents.htm?dtl%2F29597%2FIndiaFrance_Joint_Vision_for_Space_Cooperation_New_Delhi_10_March_2018=
• [Example] TRISHNA will monitor crop water stress, irrigation needs, water resources, urban ecosystems and glaciers. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2276117&reg=3&lang=1
• [Example] Cooperation includes NavIC ground station development in France and French support for Gaganyaan. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2258715&reg=3&lang=1
• [Way forward] India and France commemorated 50 years of space cooperation with joint stamps; expand into earth observation, launch and exploration. https://www.isro.gov.in/france-and-italy.html
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] TRISHNA is a joint thermal infrared earth observation mission of ISRO and which agency? (CNES, France).
[Mains 2027] How do joint earth observation missions like TRISHNA serve India's water and agricultural planning? Discuss with India-France space ties. (GS3, 10)

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Parliament and State legislatures: structure, functioning, conduct of business, powers and privileges › Parliament sessions — Article 85, prorogation
CA Topic / Headline: Explainer: Parliament adjourned sine die on August 13 at the end of the Monsoon Session but has not been prorogued, the longest unprorogued period on record. Article 85 requires that six months not pass between two sessions. Why it matters: executive control over sessions.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Article 85(1): the President summons each House, but six months shall not intervene between two sessions. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-85-sessions-of-parliament-prorogation-and-dissolution/
• Article 85(2): the President may prorogue the Houses or either House and dissolve the Lok Sabha. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-85-sessions-of-parliament-prorogation-and-dissolution/
• Article 196(3): a Bill pending in a State Legislature does not lapse on prorogation. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/articles/article-196-provisions-as-to-introduction-and-passing-of-bills/
• The Government of India Act, 1935 also provided that a pending Bill would not lapse on prorogation of the Chambers. https://www.constitutionofindia.net/historical-constitution/government-of-india-act-1935/
• The Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs decides on convening Parliament; the President formalises it. https://prsindia.org/articles-by-prs-team/explained-a-look-at-how-and-when-parliament-is-convened
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] Article 85 is based on the Government of India Act, 1935, which required a session at least once in 12 months. https://prsindia.org/articles-by-prs-team/explained-a-look-at-how-and-when-parliament-is-convened
• [Data] Ambedkar's draft reduced the gap between sessions to six months and required Parliament to meet at least twice a year. https://prsindia.org/articles-by-prs-team/explained-a-look-at-how-and-when-parliament-is-convened
• [Counterpoint] The Constituent Assembly rejected letting the Speaker or Chairman summon the House if the President failed to. https://constitutionofindia.net/constitution_of_india/the_union/articles/Article%2085
• [Way forward] The power to convene Parliament rests with the government; a fixed calendar would limit this executive discretion. https://prsindia.org/articles-by-prs-team/explained-a-look-at-how-and-when-parliament-is-convened
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under Article 85, what is the maximum gap allowed between two sessions of Parliament? (Six months).
[Mains 2027] Who controls when Parliament meets? Examine summoning and prorogation under Article 85 and the case for a fixed parliamentary calendar. (GS2, 10)
[Link] Prelims 2016, 2024 (bills lapsing on prorogation), 2020 (summoning); refined to unprorogued Monsoon Session.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Internal Security › Security challenges in border areas; organised crime and terrorism › Border villages — Vibrant Villages Programme
CA Topic / Headline: Home Minister Amit Shah said people are moving back to nearly 40 villages along the international border in Arunachal Pradesh under the Vibrant Villages Programme, and launched initiatives worth over ₹5,610 crore. Why it matters: border development, reverse migration, security.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• VVP-I was approved on 15 February 2023 for villages in 46 blocks of 19 northern border districts in four States and Ladakh. https://www.mha.gov.in/index.php/scheme/vibrant-villages-programme-vvp-i
• VVP-I outlay is ₹4,800 crore for 2022-23 to 2025-26, of which ₹2,500 crore is for all-weather roads. https://www.mha.gov.in/index.php/scheme/vibrant-villages-programme-vvp-i
• VVP was launched from Kibithoo village in Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh, on 10 April 2023. https://www.mha.gov.in/index.php/scheme/vibrant-villages-programme-vvp-i
• VVP-II, a Central Sector Scheme with ₹6,839 crore to 2028-29, covers villages on other international land borders. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2118730&reg=48&lang=2
• Arunachal Pradesh has 455 of the villages identified under VVP-I, the most of any State. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2024-pdfs/LS03122024/110.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] VVP-I and VVP-II together have a combined outlay of ₹11,639 crore. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2307094&reg=48&lang=2
• [Provision] VVP focuses on livelihoods through tourism, cultural heritage, skill development, entrepreneurship and cooperatives. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2024-pdfs/LS03122024/110.pdf
• [Example] Under VVP-I, 263 tourism projects worth ₹116 crore were approved, including viewpoints and eco-tourism. https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2026-pdfs/RS25032026/3744.pdf
• [Way forward] Government frames border villages as strategic partners in security; sustain roads, power, telecom and livelihoods to retain residents. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2307094&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] From which village was the Vibrant Villages Programme launched in April 2023? (Kibithoo, Anjaw district, Arunachal Pradesh).

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Social sector and services: health, education, human resources › Food safety — FSSAI and packaged drinking water
CA Topic / Headline: FSSAI sanctioned prosecution of Bisleri International after a regulatory sample of packaged drinking water (other than mineral water) failed the prescribed bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006. Why it matters: food regulator enforcement.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (No. 34 of 2006) received assent on 23 August 2006. https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/FOOD_ACT.pdf
• FSSAI was established under Section 4 of the Act by notification dated 5 September 2008. https://fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2018/02/5a93f91301b6bFAQ_FSSAI_Act.pdf
• FSS regulations cap bromates in packaged drinking water at 0.01 mg/l. https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Chapter%202_10_BEVERAGES_Other%20than%20Dairy%20and%20Fruits%20%20Vegetables%20based.pdf
• Packaged drinking water is certified by BIS under IS 14543, with bromate tested once in six months. https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/PM-PDW-IS-14543.pdf
• Composition of the Food Authority is prescribed in Section 5 of the FSS Act. https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/RTI_Information_Section_22_01_2020.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The FSS Act consolidated food laws to create a single statutory body for standard setting and enforcement. https://fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2018/02/5a93f91301b6bFAQ_FSSAI_Act.pdf
• [Provision] The Act moved from a multi-level, multi-departmental system to a single line of command on food safety. https://fssai.gov.in/cms/about-fssai.php
• [Example] FSSAI found packaged water makers running with an FSSAI licence but no BIS mark, or vice versa, and ordered surveillance. https://fssai.gov.in/upload/media/FSSAI_News_Water_FNB_28_10_2019.pdf
• [Way forward] FSSAI directed State food safety departments to run regular enforcement and surveillance of packaged water makers. https://fssai.gov.in/upload/media/FSSAI_News_Water_FNB_28_10_2019.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] FSSAI was established under which Act, and in which year? (Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006; 2008).
[Mains 2027] Is India's food safety regime effective in policing branded products? Examine FSSAI's enforcement powers and gaps. (GS2, 10)
[Link] Prelims 2018 (FSS Act 2006 replaced PFA Act); refined to packaged water prosecution.

• [Data] India is Nepal's largest trade partner; bilateral trade crossed USD 7 billion in 2019-20, and India transits almost all Nepal's third-country trade. https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Nepal_2022.pdf
• [Example] India handed over 50,000 reconstructed houses in Gorkha and Nuwakot districts on 15 November 2021 (USD 150 million aid). https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/India-Nepal_2022.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Demarcation of Kalapani and Susta is incomplete; Kalapani decides the India-Nepal-China tri-junction. https://mea.gov.in/distinguished-lectures-detail?674=

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Polity › Functions and responsibilities of Union and States; federal structure; devolution of powers and finances up to local levels › Renaming States — Article 3, Paschim Banga
CA Topic / Headline: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari said a resolution to rename the State 'Paschim Banga', including in English, will be tabled in the Assembly on December 9 and then sent to the Centre for parliamentary and legal procedures. Why it matters: Article 3, linguistic identity.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Renaming a State needs Parliament's approval under Articles 3 and 4; the President refers the Bill to the State legislature for its views. https://prsindia.org/theprsblog/renaming-states
• The Orissa Assembly resolved on 28 August 2008 to rename the State Odisha; the Bill passed Rajya Sabha on 24 March 2011. https://prsindia.org/billtrack/the-orissa-alteration-of-name-bill-2010
• The Uttaranchal (Alteration of Name) Act, 2006 (No. 52 of 2006) renamed the State Uttarakhand. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2006/the-uttaranchal-alteration-of-name-act-2006.pdf
• Kerala Assembly passed a resolution on 24 June 2024 to rename the State 'Keralam'. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2232093&reg=3&lang=2
• The Orissa renaming also changed the language name from Oriya to Odia, via the Constitution (113th Amendment) Bill. https://prsindia.org/theprsblog/renaming-states
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] A renaming Bill amends the State's entry in the First Schedule to the Constitution. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/bills_parliament/2010/The_Orissa_Alteration_of_Name_Bill_2010.pdf
• [Provision] The Uttaranchal Act also amended the Fourth Schedule, which allots Rajya Sabha seats, to reflect the new name. https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2006/the-uttaranchal-alteration-of-name-act-2006.pdf
• [Example] For Keralam, the Union Cabinet approved a Bill which the President refers to the Kerala Assembly under the proviso to Article 3. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2232093&reg=3&lang=1
• [Way forward] Kerala's resolution tied its name to Malayalam and linguistic State formation on 1 November 1956; renaming should follow such clear State consensus. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2232093&reg=3&lang=1
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Under Article 3, whose views must the President seek before a Bill altering a State's name is introduced? (The State Legislature's).
[Mains 2027] Renaming States reflects linguistic and historical identity. Discuss the procedure under Article 3 and whether the Union should defer to State resolutions. (GS2, 10)
[Link] Mains 2018, 2022 (reorganisation of States); refined to Paschim Banga renaming proposal.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Disaster Management › Disaster and disaster management › Landslides — National Landslide Susceptibility Mapping
CA Topic / Headline: MoS Jitendra Singh told the 7th World Landslide Forum (Faridabad) that India has mapped landslide susceptibility over about 4.3 lakh sq km and inventoried nearly 91,000 historical landslides by end-2025, shifting from post-disaster relief to prevention. Why it matters: hazard zonation, early warning.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• GSI is the nodal agency for landslide studies and completed NLSM mapping at 1:50,000 scale over about 4.3 lakh sq km in 19 States/UTs. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2158420&reg=48&lang=2
• The NLSM programme was launched in 2014-15 by GSI under the Ministry of Mines. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1987753&reg=3&lang=2
• NLSM was formally launched on 5 February 2014 at the 53rd Central Geological Programming Board meeting. https://gsi.gov.in/landslide-hazard/
• Landslide-prone hilly terrain in parts of 19 States/UTs affects parts of 179 districts. https://bhusanket.gsi.gov.in/Public_Portal_News_pdf/Revised%20Note%20on%20Landslide%20Hazards%20&%20Early%20Warning_GSI_08.08.2024.cleaned.pdf
• The National Landslide Forecasting Centre (NLFC) of GSI issues landslide forecast bulletins on its Bhusanket portal. https://bhusanket.gsi.gov.in/
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] NDMA, with GSI, framed the National Landslide Risk Management Strategy (NLRMS) in 2019. https://bhusanket.gsi.gov.in/Landslide_Hazard_pdf/Strategy%20Paper%202030.cleaned.pdf
• [Data] Susceptibility maps classify areas into high, moderate and low zones by likelihood of landslide initiation. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2158420&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] GSI had inventoried 87,474 active landslides alongside the baseline susceptibility maps. https://bhusanket.gsi.gov.in/Public_Portal_News_pdf/Revised%20Note%20on%20Landslide%20Hazards%20&%20Early%20Warning_GSI_08.08.2024.cleaned.pdf
• [Way forward] GSI aims to develop an easy-to-use, effective landslide early warning system (LEWS) to reduce losses. https://bhusanket.gsi.gov.in/Public_Portal_News_pdf/Revised%20Note%20on%20Landslide%20Hazards%20&%20Early%20Warning_GSI_08.08.2024.cleaned.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which agency is nodal for landslide studies and runs the National Landslide Susceptibility Mapping programme? (Geological Survey of India).
[Mains 2027] India is moving from post-disaster relief to prevention in landslide management. Evaluate the role of susceptibility mapping and early warning systems. (GS3, 15)
[Link] Mains 2013, 2016, 2021 (landslide causes), 2019 (hazard zonation mapping); refined to completed national mapping.

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Disaster Management › Disaster and disaster management › Glacial lakes — GLOF risk, Sheshnag
CA Topic / Headline: BRO said it was widening tracks for pilgrim safety after an outcry over an earthmover deployed at the high-altitude Sheshnag lake on the Amarnath route in Anantnag; the lake is among high-risk glacial lakes under monitoring. Why it matters: fragile Himalayan ecology, GLOF risk.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• NDMA issued Guidelines on Management of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) in October 2020. https://ndma.gov.in/Reference_Material/NDMAGuidelines
• NGRMP covers Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand with ₹150 crore outlay. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2117268
• CWC monitors 477 Himalayan glacial lakes and water bodies over 50 hectares monthly in the monsoon since 2011. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1809123&reg=48&lang=2
• NDMA's Committee on Disaster Risk Reduction (CoDRR), with six Himalayan States/UTs, identified high-risk glacial lakes for expeditions. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2042990
• Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology monitors glaciers and analyses hazard triggers. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2117268
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Data] Central Electricity Authority identified 47 dams likely to be affected by GLOFs from Indian glacial lakes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2042990
• [Provision] NGRMP builds a glacial lake inventory, early warning systems and automatic weather stations for real-time monitoring. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2150261&reg=48&lang=2
• [Example] NRSC and CWC inventories support mitigation such as de-watering and controlled breaching of risky lakes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2201535&reg=48&lang=2
• [Way forward] NDMA's GLOF SOP covers pre-disaster preparedness, real-time response and recovery; apply it to works near high-risk lakes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2150828&reg=48&lang=2
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] When did NDMA issue guidelines on Management of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods? (October 2020).
[Mains 2027] Infrastructure works near Himalayan glacial lakes raise GLOF risk. Discuss India's GLOF risk mitigation framework and its gaps. (GS3, 10)
[Link] Mains 2014, 2020 (Himalayan glaciers and climate change); refined to Sheshnag lake excavation row.

Syllabus Tag: GS2 › Social Justice › Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections; mechanisms, laws, institutions and bodies for their protection › Tribal women's inheritance — Hindu Succession Act s.2(2)
CA Topic / Headline: Jharkhand High Court ruled that daughters in the Santhal community cannot be excluded from their father's property solely on traditional beliefs. Why it matters: gender justice vs customary law for Scheduled Tribes.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• Section 2(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 says the Act does not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/520/520_2017_5_1501_40564_Judgement_09-Dec-2022.pdf
• SC (2022): denying succession to ST women would deprive them of the right to livelihood under Article 21. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/520/520_2017_5_1501_40564_Judgement_09-Dec-2022.pdf
• SC asked the Central Government to consider withdrawing the HSA exemption for Scheduled Tribes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2244946&reg=3&lang=1
• SC (2025 INSC 865) heard a Gond woman's heirs claiming an equal share in her father's property. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2023/3486/3486_2023_13_1501_62514_Judgement_17-Jul-2025.pdf
• SC (2024 INSC 1005) directed the Centre to examine withdrawing the HSA exemption for Scheduled Tribes. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2019/22266/22266_2019_9_1508_58088_Judgement_19-Dec-2024.pdf
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Judgment] SC (Madhu Kishwar case): excluding tribal women from inheritance under customary law, based solely on sex, is discriminatory. https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/15685.pdf
• [Example] In the 2022 case an ST daughter claimed a share of land acquisition compensation; respondents cited Section 2(2). https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2017/520/520_2017_5_1501_40564_Judgement_09-Dec-2022.pdf
• [Counterpoint] Courts deny claims where plaintiffs fail to prove community custom granting daughters rights. https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2023/3486/3486_2023_13_1501_62514_Judgement_17-Jul-2025.pdf
• [Way forward] SC directed the Centre to decide whether to amend the HSA to cover Scheduled Tribes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2244946&reg=3&lang=1
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] Which section of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 excludes Scheduled Tribe members from its application? (Section 2(2)).
[Mains 2027] Customary law often denies tribal women inheritance. Should the Hindu Succession Act exemption for Scheduled Tribes be withdrawn? Discuss. (GS2, 10)

Syllabus Tag: GS3 › Science & Technology › Achievements of Indians in S&T; indigenisation of technology › Anti-submarine warfare — ASW Shallow Water Craft (Ashank)
CA Topic / Headline: The Indian Navy received Ashank, an indigenously designed anti-submarine warfare shallow water craft built by GRSE, Kolkata, at Visakhapatnam; it carries lightweight torpedoes, rocket launchers and advanced sonar. Why it matters: littoral ASW, Aatmanirbharta in shipbuilding.
Prelims Recall (CSE 2027):
• INS Arnala, the first of sixteen ASW-SWC ships, was commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 18 June 2025. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2134607
• GRSE builds eight ASW SWCs; Arnala was built under a PPP with L&T Shipbuilders, Kattupalli. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2137224&reg=48&lang=2
• Arnala-class ships replace the Abhay-class ASW corvettes. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1909308&reg=48&lang=2
• INS Arnala is 77 m long, the largest naval warship propelled by a diesel engine-waterjet combination. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2137263&reg=48&lang=2
• ASW SWCs carry over 80% indigenous content. https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1885185
Mains Recall (CSE 2027):
• [Provision] The ships do sub-surface surveillance, search and rescue, Low Intensity Maritime Operations and mine laying in littoral waters. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1909308&reg=48&lang=2
• [Data] Sensors include hull-mounted sonar and Low Frequency Variable Depth Sonar, with torpedoes, ASW rockets and NSG-30 gun. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2146420
• [Example] INS Arnala, Androth and Mahe were inducted in 2025, part of the Navy's Aatmanirbhar journey. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/dec/doc2025123716101.pdf
• [Way forward] Armed forces have identified over 5,000 items to source domestically; extend this to sonars and weapons. https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/dec/doc2025123716101.pdf
Relevance & Revision Note:
[Prelims 2027] How many ASW Shallow Water Craft are being inducted, and which class do they replace? (Sixteen; Abhay-class corvettes).
[Mains 2027] Shallow-water ASW craft strengthen India's coastal defence. Discuss their role and the shift from a buyer's to a builder's navy. (GS3, 10)
